title: Aadhaar in or out? Mixed messaging puzzles voters
description: Voters are caught in a dilemma as BLOs decline Aadhaar for voter verification, opting for class 10 marks cards instead. Officials clarify that Aadhaar is solely for identity purposes, not for validating age or address. While voters can submit Aadhaar alongsid…
content: BENGALURU: Aadhaar is officially on the list of documents accepted for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) verification, but on the ground, several voters say BLOs are turning it down and asking for class 10 marks cards instead during hearings. The contradictory instructions have sent voters scrambling for extra paperwork, fearing repeat trips to verification centres if what they carry is not accepted. Officials from the office of the chief electoral officer (CEO), Karnataka, clarified Aadhaar is meant for identity verification, not as proof of age or address. It can, however, be submitted alongside any of the 11 other documents listed on the reverse of the enumeration form, and the ERO has the discretion to seek up to three documents from a voter. Explaining why Aadhaar is treated differently, a senior official said, “Unlike other documents, Aadhaar can be edited time and again. This is not easily possible with the other documents listed.” Fresh voter applications add to BLO burden BLA-2 from CV Raman Nagar, Vinu Jade, offered another reason for the caution around Aadhaar: those from Nepal are also issued Aadhaar cards, though short-duration ones meant only to permit them to work in India. “Hence, Aadhaar in the SIR process only serves the purpose of validating one’s mobile number. It’s not considered as a document submitted for proof of citizenship,” he said. The document trouble has spilled into the online process too. A voter flagged a glitch in the ECI portal’s Aadhaar name-validation logic, which reportedly blocks those with single names from submitting Form 8 online even when the entered name matches their Aadhaar exactly. The confusion comes as the window for filing claims and objections closes on Sept 23. After that, hearings on notices already issued will continue until Oct 22. A week after he received his notice, a voter from RR Nagar said he got a call from his BLO asking him not to bring Aadhaar along with his passport. “I was instead asked to produce my class 10 marks card during my hearing, scheduled this week. To be on the safer side, I have now got copies of all my marks cards to avoid having to return to the centre again for lack of documents,” he said. He added that the BLO told him certain details of non-nationals had been uploaded and flagged by higher-ups during document verification. When TOI reached out to the CEO’s office, officials denied being aware of any such cases and said a voter could write in for clarification from the ERO and BLO concerned. A second voter, from Old Airport Road, said he had come prepared with his Aadhaar card but was similarly asked to submit his class 10 marks card as the second document.

title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% in August as fuel prices rise
description:
Britain’s annual inflation rate rose to 3.1% in August, up from 2.9%, driven by higher fuel prices linked to the Middle East war, official data shows.

Read More: https://punchng.com/uk-inflation-jumps-to-3-1-in-august-as-fuel-prices-rise/
content: Britain’s annual inflation rate climbed in line with analysts’ expectations in August, official data showed Wednesday, as the Middle East war drove up fuel prices. The Consumer Prices Index rose 3.1 per cent in the 12 months to August, up from 2.9 per cent the previous month, the Office for National Statistics said. Higher inflation adds pressure on Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his finance minister John Healey to ease the cost of living for households ahead of the Labour government’s budget update next month. The Bank of England is forecast to maintain its benchmark interest rate at 3.75 percent on Thursday as the UK economy struggles for growth. To tackle persistently high consumer prices, the US Federal Reserve is expected Wednesday to also lift borrowing costs, following a similar move by the European Central Bank last week. With central bank interest rates on the rise — and government bond yields reaching multi-decade highs in recent weeks — Healey has pledged to maintain strict fiscal discipline. But he has not been drawn on whether this means his budget on October 28 will include new tax rises. Analysts expect inflation to rise towards the end of the year as higher energy costs feed through to bills further, with little sign of a deal to end the Middle East war. “With the situation in the Middle East looking increasingly fraught, the expectation is that inflation will continue to climb higher until the end of the year at a minimum,” said Richard Carter, head of fixed interest research at Quilter Cheviot. “For the government, today’s figures are a kick in the teeth for an administration that wants to make easing the cost of living its central mission,” he added. AFP

title: Indonesia prepares regulation to tighten subsidized fuel access
description: Indonesia's Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry is drafting a regulation to restrict the distribution of subsidized fuels, such as Pertalite and ...
content: “Yes, it is true that we are formulating the regulation,” Minister Bahlil Lahadalia told the press after a meeting with Commission XII of the House of Representatives (DPR) in Jakarta on Wednesday. He highlighted the planned policy while reiterating his call for citizens deemed economically privileged to refrain from consuming Pertalite and Biosolar, giving more space to those in need. “To my fellow citizens who are well-off or own good cars, let us refrain from using subsidized fuels because those products are dedicated to our deserving brothers and sisters,” Bahlil said. He also alluded to reports of long queues for fuel in Makassar, South Sulawesi, stressing that the country is not facing a shortage, with fuel supplies staying at the national minimum threshold, sufficient for 18 to 20 days. With that in mind, Bahlil suspected that the Makassar queues might have been caused by misuse of subsidized fuels. “Long queues can be caused by many factors. Among them is that there are people who line up at filling stations with ulterior motives,” he said. The minister earlier noted a plan to restrict Pertalite sales for residents in the top two strata of the National Single Socioeconomic Data (DTSEN), saying the move was pending data validation to ensure accuracy. Responding to the plan, Pertamina Patra Niaga Corporate Secretary Roberth Dumatubun said the company stands ready to support restricted access to Pertalite and Biosolar for citizens in the top two strata. Pertamina awaits the government's policy and will follow official instructions as a state-run energy firm, he stated. title: India to add 3,860 MW data centre capacity by 2030, require USD 29.9 bn investment: Report - The Tribune
description: India's data centre sector is set for a major capacity expansion, with 3,860 MW of new capacity expected to come up by 2030, including 509 MW already under construction and 3,351 MW in the planning stage, according to a report by Cushman & Wakefield.
content: New Delhi [India], September 16 (ANI): India's data centre sector is set for a major capacity expansion, with 3,860 MW of new capacity expected to come up by 2030, including 509 MW already under construction and 3,351 MW in the planning stage, according to a report by Cushman & Wakefield. The expansion is expected to require USD 29.9 billion in development capital through 2030, placing India among the major data centre investment markets in the Asia Pacific region, the report said. India's operational data centre capacity stood at 1,789 MW as of H1 2026, up from around 400 MW in 2019. The country's top seven markets added 178 MW of capacity during the first half of 2026, while colocation vacancy stood at 14.9%. Mumbai remains the country's largest data centre market, accounting for 50% of operational capacity at 890 MW. It also has the largest upcoming pipeline at around 1.7 GW as of H1 2026, with the city expected to cross 1 GW of operational capacity by end-2026, the report said. However, capacity expansion is increasingly spreading across other major hubs. Hyderabad has 151 MW of operational capacity and 710 MW of upcoming supply, while Chennai has 214 MW operational capacity and 368 MW of upcoming supply. Delhi NCR has 183 MW operational capacity and 387 MW of future supply. The report said India's relatively low data centre penetration, growing enterprise use of artificial intelligence and increasing hyperscaler activity leave significant room for future expansion. It also noted that AI-focused infrastructure is driving demand for facilities with higher rack densities. Cushman & Wakefield Executive Managing Director Gautam Saraf said, “With nearly 3.9 GW of additional capacity expected across the country's leading markets by 2030, this deeper ecosystem will be critical in supporting the next phase of cloud adoption, AI deployment and data-driven growth across the economy.” At the Asia Pacific level, data centre capacity is projected to increase 2.7 times by 2030, requiring more than USD 280 billion in capital expenditure. India is expected to account for nearly USD 29.9 billion of this development investment, the report said. The report also flagged sustainability as an increasing planning priority, as the rapid expansion of AI workloads is expected to raise data centre energy demand and resource requirements. (ANI) (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

title: How do you introduce a dog to an autistic child?
description: How To Introduce a Dog to an Autistic Child: A Comprehensive Guide Successfully introducing a dog to an autistic child requires careful planning, patience, and a deep understanding of both the child’s and the dog’s needs; How do you introduce a dog to an auti…
content: Successfully introducing a dog to an autistic child requires careful planning, patience, and a deep understanding of both the child’s and the dog’s needs; How do you introduce a dog to an autistic child? It’s achieved through gradual, structured interactions, focusing on safety, creating positive associations, and respecting boundaries to foster a beneficial and harmonious relationship. The bond between a child and a dog can be incredibly powerful, offering numerous benefits. However, for autistic children, the introduction process requires extra sensitivity and awareness. - Potential Benefits: A well-matched and well-introduced dog can provide: - Emotional support and companionship: Dogs can offer unconditional love and reduce feelings of loneliness or anxiety. - Improved social skills: Interacting with a dog can help develop communication and social skills, as children learn to interpret the dog’s body language and respond appropriately. - Sensory regulation: The tactile experience of petting a dog can be calming and provide sensory input. - Increased physical activity: Dog ownership encourages walks and playtime, promoting physical health. - Responsibility and routine: Caring for a dog can instill a sense of responsibility and help establish a daily routine. - Potential Challenges: It’s important to acknowledge the potential difficulties: - Sensory sensitivities: Autistic children may be sensitive to the dog’s barking, licking, shedding, or strong smells. - Communication difficulties: Interpreting the dog’s needs and communicating effectively can be challenging. - Unexpected behaviors: The dog’s unpredictable movements or behaviors may cause anxiety or overwhelm. - Difficulty with boundaries: Setting and maintaining appropriate boundaries with the dog may be difficult. - Hyperfocus: The child may hyperfocus on the dog, neglecting other activities or responsibilities. How do you introduce a dog to an autistic child? This requires a phased approach, prioritizing safety and comfort at every stage. - Preparation is Key: Before bringing the dog home: - Gather information: Learn about the child’s specific sensory sensitivities, communication style, and comfort levels. - Dog selection: Choose a dog with a calm, predictable temperament, ideally one that has experience with children. - Home preparation: Create a safe space for the dog, such as a crate or designated room, where it can retreat when feeling overwhelmed. - Sensory familiarization: Introduce the child to dog-related smells and sounds gradually, using recordings or scent samples. - The First Meeting: Keep the initial encounter short and controlled: - Neutral territory: If possible, arrange the first meeting in a neutral environment, such as a park, to reduce territoriality. - Leash control: Keep the dog on a leash to ensure safety and prevent chasing or jumping. - Distance: Start with a significant distance between the child and the dog, gradually decreasing it as the child feels comfortable. - Positive reinforcement: Reward the child for calm behavior and positive interactions, such as gentle petting or speaking in a quiet voice. - No pressure: Never force the child to interact with the dog. Allow them to approach at their own pace. - Introducing the Dog to the Home: Gradual acclimation to the home environment is vital: - Controlled access: Initially, limit the dog’s access to certain areas of the house, especially the child’s bedroom or personal space. - Scent exchange: Allow the child to become familiar with the dog’s scent by introducing a blanket or toy that the dog has used. - Supervised interactions: Always supervise interactions between the child and the dog, especially in the early stages. - Quiet time: Ensure the dog has plenty of quiet time to rest and adjust to its new surroundings. - Building a Relationship: Encouraging positive interactions is key for bonding: - Structured activities: Engage the child and dog in structured activities, such as playing fetch or going for short walks. - Positive reinforcement: Continue to reward both the child and the dog for positive interactions. - Teach the child: Provide clear and simple instructions on how to interact with the dog appropriately, such as gentle petting and avoiding pulling on the ears or tail. - Respect boundaries: Teach the child to respect the dog’s boundaries and recognize signs of stress or discomfort. Understanding common mistakes can improve the success of the introduction. - Rushing the process: A gradual introduction is crucial. Don’t force the child or the dog to interact before they are ready. - Ignoring sensory sensitivities: Be mindful of the child’s sensory sensitivities and avoid overwhelming them with loud noises, strong smells, or sudden movements. - Lack of supervision: Never leave the child and dog unsupervised, especially in the early stages of the relationship. - Ignoring the dog’s needs: Ensure the dog’s needs for exercise, rest, and quiet time are met. - Expecting too much too soon: Building a strong bond takes time and patience. How long should the initial meeting between the child and the dog last? The first meeting should be very brief, no more than 5-10 minutes. The goal is to create a positive first impression without overwhelming either the child or the dog. Observe their body language carefully and end the interaction before either party shows signs of stress or discomfort. What if the child is afraid of dogs? If the child is afraid of dogs, a more gradual approach is necessary. Start by exposing them to pictures or videos of dogs from a distance. Then, consider having them interact with a therapy dog or a very calm, well-trained dog in a controlled environment, with the guidance of a professional. How do you teach an autistic child to be gentle with a dog? Use simple, clear instructions and positive reinforcement. For example, you can say, “Gentle hands,” while gently guiding the child’s hand to pet the dog softly. Reward them with praise or a small treat when they interact with the dog appropriately. Role-playing can also be helpful. What are the signs that the dog is stressed or overwhelmed? Signs of stress in a dog include: panting, yawning, lip licking, whale eye (showing the whites of their eyes), tucked tail, flattened ears, and avoiding eye contact. If you observe any of these signs, immediately separate the child and the dog. What if the dog barks excessively? Excessive barking can be triggering for autistic children. Address the underlying cause of the barking, such as boredom, anxiety, or territoriality. Provide the dog with plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and training to reduce barking. Consider consulting with a professional dog trainer or behaviorist. Can a service dog or therapy dog help an autistic child? Yes, both service dogs and therapy dogs can provide significant benefits to autistic children. Service dogs are trained to perform specific tasks to assist individuals with disabilities, such as providing deep pressure therapy or preventing wandering. Therapy dogs provide emotional support and comfort in various settings. What are the key differences between a service dog and a therapy dog? The key difference lies in their training and purpose. Service dogs are individually trained to perform specific tasks for individuals with disabilities and have legal protections under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Therapy dogs provide emotional support and comfort in various settings, but do not have the same legal protections. What should I do if the child tries to hug or kiss the dog excessively? Hugging and kissing can be overwhelming for dogs. Teach the child alternative ways to show affection, such as gentle petting, speaking in a soft voice, or offering a treat. Explain to the child that the dog prefers to be petted rather than hugged. How can I prevent the dog from jumping on the child? Train the dog to sit or stay when greeting people. Use positive reinforcement to reward the dog for calm behavior. If the dog jumps, redirect its attention to a different activity. Consistency is key to preventing jumping. What if the dog steals the child’s toys? Teach the dog the “leave it” command. When the dog attempts to take a toy, say “leave it” and offer a higher-value treat. This will teach the dog to associate leaving the toy with a positive reward. Store the child’s toys in a place where the dog cannot access them. How do you introduce a dog to an autistic child who has sensory processing issues? When introducing a dog to an autistic child with sensory processing issues, it’s important to minimize sensory overload. Keep initial interactions short and quiet, and avoid strong smells or bright lights. Gradually introduce the dog’s presence and sounds, while closely monitoring the child’s reaction. What type of training is best for a dog living with an autistic child? Focus on basic obedience training to ensure the dog is well-behaved and responsive to commands. Socialization is also crucial to help the dog become comfortable in different environments and around various people and animals. Consider working with a trainer who has experience working with dogs and autistic children.

title: Saudi Arabia shoots down Houthi drone strike outside of Mecca
description: The attacks on Saudi Arabia have shocked global energy markets roiled by the six-month US-Iran war, which has slowed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to a trickle.
content: Saudi Arabia’s air defenses destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen said on Wednesday, as fighting spreads in the Middle East. The drone, intercepted on Tuesday evening, was the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca after a ballistic missile launch in July 2017, spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a statement, and follows a week of attacks from Iran-aligned Houthi fighters that have drawn Saudi Arabia deeper into the war. Mecca is home to some of the holiest sites in Islam and the focal point of the annual hajj pilgrimage, and its security was a “red line,” the coalition spokesperson al-Malki said in the statement. Houthi officials have denied targeting Mecca. The attacks on Saudi Arabia have shocked global energy markets roiled by the six-month US-Iran war, which has slowed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to a trickle. The Houthis have seized control of parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in recent days overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb, one of the world’s most important shipping straits, threatening Saudi Arabia’s oil exports rerouted from the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia issued security alerts for Mecca on Tuesday, but Houthi political bureau member Mohammed al-Farah denied the group had targeted the city, calling the allegation “an outright lie” in comments carried by the Houthi-run SABA news agency. The Houthis have announced several major attacks on Saudi Arabia over the past week, including attacks on an air base on Monday, which they said were in retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen. The air base attack wounded 13 civilians, Saudi-led military coalition officials said. Saudi Arabia has blamed a separate pro-Iranian movement, based in Iraq, for an attack on Friday that knocked out one of the kingdom’s most important oil transport routes, the East-West Pipeline across the Arabian desert. The 745-mile East-West Pipeline linking Saudi Arabia’s Gulf oil fields to the Red Sea has been the kingdom’s principal export route while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted by nearly seven months of war, which has killed thousands of people across the region. Since the pipeline was shut after Friday’s attack, traders say a prolonged closure could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume. But US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days. Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quieted under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis pushed back forces aligned with the Yemeni government this month. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned US President Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid.

title: Why Samsung Is Betting $231 Million on Dutch AI Inference Chip Startup Euclyd to Directly Rival Nvidia
description: Samsung co-led a $231 million funding round for Dutch startup Euclyd, seeking exposure to AI inference chips, memory-centric architecture and alternatives to Nvidia's market dominance.
content: EINDHOVEN, Netherlands — Samsung Electronics has co-led a $231 million funding round for Euclyd, a two-year-old Dutch startup building specialized chips for AI inference, marking the South Korean electronics giant's latest move to establish a foothold in the fast-growing market for alternatives to Nvidia's dominant AI processors. Here is why Samsung made the bet, based on public statements from the companies involved. Euclyd, founded in 2024 by Bernardo Kastrup and Atul Sinha at High Tech Campus Eindhoven, raised more than 200 million euros in its Series A round, with the financing co-led by Samsung alongside Somerset Capital Partners, the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, and Innovation Industries. The exact size of Samsung's individual contribution has not been disclosed. The first and most fundamental reason behind Samsung's interest is where Euclyd has chosen to compete. Rather than building chips for the resource-intensive process of training AI models, where Nvidia's dominance is closest to a monopoly, Euclyd is focused specifically on inference, the stage at which an already-trained AI model responds to live user queries. Nvidia's share of the inference chip segment has been estimated at between 60% and 75% as of 2025, a commanding position but one industry analysts view as considerably more contestable than Nvidia's grip on training hardware, giving challengers like Euclyd a more realistic opening. A second reason ties directly to Samsung's own core business. Euclyd's chip architecture is built around what the company describes as processor-memory co-design, an approach that treats memory bandwidth and system-level architecture as just as central to performance as the processor itself. Because Samsung is one of the world's largest memory chip manufacturers, an inference architecture built around tighter memory integration plays directly to Samsung's existing manufacturing and engineering strengths, rather than requiring the company to compete purely on general-purpose processor design against far more established rivals. Euclyd's own founder pointed to that alignment as a central part of what makes Samsung's involvement valuable beyond the capital itself. "Samsung can help us in more ways than money," Kastrup said. "They are one of the biggest memory manufacturers in the world. They do a lot of engineering, they know a lot about systems, they know the supply chain, they have a huge network." That combination of manufacturing scale, systems engineering expertise and established supply chain relationships gives Euclyd resources a typical venture-backed startup would struggle to access on its own, while giving Samsung early visibility and influence over an architecture built specifically to leverage its own memory technology. A third reason reflects broader industry dynamics around the rising cost of AI infrastructure. Kastrup has framed Euclyd's mission explicitly around addressing those cost and energy pressures. "AI is becoming a foundation of economic growth, scientific discovery, and national competitiveness, but its potential will remain constrained unless we fundamentally change the infrastructure beneath it," Kastrup said. For Samsung, backing a company aimed at reducing the energy consumption and cost of running AI models aligns with the broader industry push to make large-scale AI deployment more economically sustainable, a trend that, if successful, could expand overall demand for the memory and systems components Samsung supplies regardless of whether Euclyd's own chips achieve widespread adoption. A fourth factor is diversification against overreliance on any single AI hardware supplier. Samsung's investment comes amid a broader wave of spending by major technology companies on alternatives to Nvidia's GPUs, with Google, Amazon Web Services, Meta and OpenAI all separately developing custom AI silicon. OpenAI disclosed its first custom chip, code-named Jalapeño, in August, claiming industry-leading efficiency gains over general-purpose GPUs. By backing Euclyd, Samsung positions itself on the investor side of that broader shift away from GPU dependence, rather than solely as a component supplier reacting to decisions made by chip designers elsewhere. A fifth reason involves access to Europe's semiconductor ecosystem and talent base. Euclyd's board is chaired by Peter Wennink, the former president and chief executive officer of Dutch lithography equipment maker ASML, whose machines are essential to advanced chip manufacturing worldwide. Wennink has said Europe's underlying semiconductor capabilities position Euclyd to compete on a global scale, a statement that reflects the deep pool of chip engineering expertise concentrated around the Eindhoven region, home to ASML and a dense cluster of semiconductor suppliers and research institutions. A sixth reason relates to timing and stage of investment. Backing Euclyd at the Series A stage gives Samsung an early position, and likely board-level influence, in a company still years away from commercial deployment, rather than competing to invest at a later, more expensive stage once the startup's technology and market fit are more proven. Euclyd has said it aims to deploy its first physical AI chip systems in 2028 and to serve thousands of enterprise customers by 2030, giving Samsung a multi-year runway to help shape the company's direction as it approaches commercialization. A seventh reason concerns Euclyd's dual business model, which combines direct hardware and rack system sales to enterprise customers seeking on-premises AI inference capacity with a separate revenue stream from licensing its underlying chip architecture to other manufacturers. That licensing path offers Samsung a potential future avenue to incorporate Euclyd's inference architecture into its own broader product and manufacturing ecosystem, beyond the direct equity stake itself. An eighth reason is straightforward market growth. As AI adoption shifts from an initial phase dominated by model training toward sustained, large-scale deployment, inference workloads are expected to represent a rapidly expanding share of total AI compute demand over the coming years, giving early investors in credible inference-focused hardware companies exposure to that anticipated shift. A ninth reason is risk-sharing. By co-investing alongside established venture and growth-equity firms including Somerset Capital Partners, EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund and Innovation Industries, Samsung shares both the financial risk and the due-diligence work involved in backing an unproven, pre-commercial hardware startup, rather than bearing that risk entirely on its own balance sheet. A tenth and final reason is optionality. Euclyd remains years from any commercial deployment, and Kastrup himself has acknowledged the company's technology is unproven at scale. For Samsung, the investment functions as a relatively contained financial bet on a plausible challenger to Nvidia's dominance in a segment of the AI chip market Samsung has a direct interest in seeing diversify, without requiring Samsung to abandon or compete directly against its own existing chip and memory manufacturing relationships with other AI hardware developers in the meantime. © Copyright 2026 IBTimes AU. content: GE Vernova T&D India shares fell nearly 9% over the two sessions, while CG Power declined 8%. Hitachi Energy shares were down around 6%, while Sterlite Tech and HFCL tumbled 10% each. TD Power Systems shares crashed 16% during the period. These stocks have rallied sharply in recent months, gaining up to 63% in 2026 so far, amid expectations of rising demand for power generation, transmission and distribution to support India’s data centre boom. Also read | Rs 1.13 lakh crore boom in one corner, a bust in another: What changed in the AI trade? AI slowdown calls Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in a long X post on Saturday, called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence. The Anthropic CEO wrote that in nearly a year, AI agents "could be capable of taking over the entire internet, potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage." We Must Pace the Frontier: I’ve written a new essay on why the AI industry should slow down, with a three-part plan for doing so. Anthropic is unilaterally committing to the first of these steps. We’ll provide third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our… There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid. First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and… https://t.co/GK7XcoOh3v AI bubble worries While artificial intelligence has brought in a new wave of technological innovations, it also brought in concerns around the excessive optimism around it, with analysts even doubting if it is just a bubble ready to be popped and wreak havoc on the financial market. Earlier this year, popular American investor Michael Burry wrote on a Substack post that he sees many indicators, both technical and fundamental, lining up for the same conclusion as the Dotcom crash. "1999 went where no market had gone before, and I would say so can this one...It is already there on a number of indicators," he said, arguing that massive venture capital flows, rising AI debt issuance, and extreme market optimism are creating conditions where valuations may detach from economic reality. title: In 2006, an artist installed 75 human figures off Grenada after a hurricane damaged its reefs; corals later colonized them alongside parrotfish, shrimp and fireworms
description: After Hurricane Ivan wreaked havoc on Molinere Bay's coral reefs in Grenada, expert efforts saw the installation of concrete sculptures. A recent analysis found that these artificial reefs are nurturing coral growth similar to their natural counterparts. Fire…
content: A reef born from disaster Molinere Bay was never intended to be an art gallery. Taylor built the underwater park in response to the damage Hurricane Ivan caused to the reef in this area, leaving too little hard structure left for coral to grow on. Taylor used pH-neutral, textured concrete to create the sculptures, giving coral polyps a surface on which to settle. According to Grenada's Tourism Authority, the park opened its doors to tourists in May 2006, having placed 75 statues of people on the seabed occupying an area of about 800 square meters, at depths of five to eight meters. It has since expanded, and it now sits on National Geographic's list of 25 Wonders of the World. A ring built to face the current, together. Image Credits: @jasondecairestaylor/Instagram Watching bare concrete disappear under coral is not instant magic, and usually follows a fairly predictable pattern. It's worth being clear that the following data doesn't come from Taylor's statues themselves: to follow this process, researchers from Wisconsin Lutheran College studied a different concrete structure in the same Moliniere-Beauséjour Marine Protected Area, a set of artificial reef "pyramids" built separately by local conservation volunteers. The study found that the fire coral, a fast-spreading species that can quickly regenerate after storm damage, tends to be one of the first settlers to establish itself on any newly formed concrete structure in Grenadian waters before other types of coral start to settle there. The study also found that these artificial reefs had far less harmful algae than natural reefs and more coralline algae, which helps coral larvae attach and grow. Thus, a properly constructed concrete reef in this bay may support coral growth better, at least initially, than some nearby natural reefs. Parrotfish, shrimp and fireworms move in Still recognizably human, just barely. Image Credits: @jasondecairestaylor/Instagram Grenada had good reason to want its coral back quickly. Research published in the Journal of Environmental Management studied Grenville Bay on Grenada's coast directly and found that healthy coral reefs there helped keep the shoreline stable by dissipating wave energy before it reached land, while reef degradation elsewhere in the same bay was linked to severe erosion and flooding. The destruction of the coral reefs in Molinere Bay by Hurricane Ivan meant the coastline lost some of its natural protection. Reconstructing that protective wall, even if it was not biological, was something for Molinere Bay to start with. A quiet success story, with limits This doesn’t mean that concrete statues can totally replace a living reef. The Grenada pyramid study is careful to note that the diversity of corals on the artificial structures it studied was still lower than on nearby natural reefs, and that longer-term monitoring is needed to know how they do over decades. But as an emergency response to hurricane damage, the Molinere Bay sculptures have achieved an unusual conservation outcome. They took disaster recovery and turned it into an ecosystem that actually works and that people want to visit. Two decades after the first figures were submerged, they are barely recognizable as human forms, and that is exactly the point. title: Does ferret poop smell?
description: Does Ferret Poop Smell? Understanding and Managing Ferret Odor Yes, ferret poop does indeed smell, and its distinctive odor can be quite strong; however, with proper care and hygiene, the scent can be effectively managed. Introduction: Ferret Odor Demystified…
content: Yes, ferret poop does indeed smell, and its distinctive odor can be quite strong; however, with proper care and hygiene, the scent can be effectively managed. Ferrets, with their playful antics and endearing personalities, have become increasingly popular pets. However, prospective ferret owners are often concerned about one particular aspect: their odor. While ferrets do possess a natural musky scent, the smell of their waste products, particularly their feces, is often a primary concern. Understanding the factors contributing to ferret poop odor and implementing effective management strategies are crucial for ensuring a harmonious living environment for both ferret and owner. Does ferret poop smell? This is a question on the minds of many contemplating ferret ownership, and the answer, while initially daunting, is manageable with the right approach. Several factors contribute to the intensity and unpleasantness of ferret poop odor. These include diet, hygiene practices, and the ferret’s overall health. Addressing each of these areas is critical for minimizing the smell. - Diet: A ferret’s diet plays a significant role in the quality and odor of its feces. Ferrets are obligate carnivores, meaning their bodies are designed to digest animal protein. Diets high in carbohydrates, fiber, or plant-based ingredients can lead to digestive upset, resulting in softer, smellier stools. - Hygiene: Regular cleaning of the ferret’s cage, including the litter box, is essential. Ferret poop left to accumulate quickly becomes a breeding ground for bacteria, intensifying the odor. - Health: Certain medical conditions, such as intestinal parasites or digestive disorders, can also contribute to increased fecal odor. If you notice a significant change in your ferret’s poop consistency or smell, consulting a veterinarian is crucial. - Age: Young ferrets (kits) sometimes have more difficulty digesting food, leading to more pungent waste. This usually resolves as they mature. Proper litter box management is paramount in controlling ferret poop odor. - Choosing the Right Litter: Select a ferret-safe litter that effectively absorbs moisture and controls odor. Avoid clay-based litters, as these can be dusty and potentially harmful if ingested. Paper-based, wood pellet, or wheat-based litters are generally good choices. - Regular Cleaning: Scoop the litter box at least once a day, preferably twice, to remove solid waste. Completely empty and clean the litter box with soap and water at least once a week. - Litter Box Placement: Position the litter box in a well-ventilated area to help dissipate odors. Ferrets often prefer to eliminate in corners, so placing the litter box in a corner of the cage can encourage proper litter box habits. - Multiple Litter Boxes: For multiple ferrets or larger cages, providing multiple litter boxes can help reduce odor and ensure that all ferrets have easy access to a designated elimination area. The diet of your ferret significantly impacts the smell of its waste. - High-Quality Protein: Feed your ferret a high-quality ferret food that is primarily composed of animal protein (at least 30-40%). - Limited Fiber: Keep the fiber content of the food relatively low (less than 3%). High fiber can lead to digestive upset. - Avoid Sugars and Carbohydrates: Minimize the amount of sugars and carbohydrates in your ferret’s diet. These ingredients are difficult for ferrets to digest and can contribute to increased fecal odor. - Treats in Moderation: Offer treats sparingly, and choose treats that are specifically formulated for ferrets and are low in sugar and carbohydrates. Beyond the litter box, other aspects of ferret hygiene contribute to overall odor control. - Cage Cleaning: Regularly clean the entire ferret cage, including bedding, toys, and food dishes. - Bathing (Sparingly): While ferrets groom themselves, occasional bathing can help reduce body odor. However, avoid over-bathing, as this can strip the ferret’s skin of its natural oils and lead to increased oil production and muskier odor. Bathe only when necessary, using a ferret-specific shampoo or a mild, unscented baby shampoo. - Ear Cleaning: Ferrets produce earwax, which can contribute to odor. Clean your ferret’s ears regularly with a ferret-specific ear cleaner. - Teeth Cleaning: Poor dental hygiene can also contribute to bad breath and overall odor. Brush your ferret’s teeth regularly with a ferret-specific toothbrush and toothpaste. Several common mistakes can exacerbate ferret poop odor. - Using the Wrong Litter: As mentioned earlier, avoid clay-based litters. - Infrequent Cleaning: Neglecting to clean the litter box and cage regularly is a major contributor to odor. - Overfeeding: Overfeeding can lead to digestive upset and increased fecal output. - Improper Diet: Feeding a diet that is not appropriate for ferrets can lead to digestive problems and increased odor. - Using Scented Products: Avoid using heavily scented litters, cage cleaners, or shampoos, as these can irritate your ferret and may not effectively mask the odor. Effectively managing ferret poop odor requires a holistic approach that addresses diet, hygiene, and health. By implementing the strategies outlined above, ferret owners can significantly reduce the odor associated with their pets and enjoy a cleaner, more pleasant living environment. Addressing the question of Does ferret poop smell? ultimately hinges on proactive and consistent care. How often should I clean my ferret’s litter box? You should scoop the litter box at least once a day, preferably twice. A complete cleaning, involving emptying and scrubbing the entire box with soap and water, should be done at least once a week. This regular cleaning schedule prevents the build-up of bacteria and minimizes odor. What is the best type of litter for ferrets? The best types of litter for ferrets are those that are safe, absorbent, and effective at controlling odor. Paper-based, wood pellet, or wheat-based litters are generally good choices. Avoid clay-based litters as they can be dusty and potentially harmful if ingested. What kind of food should I feed my ferret to reduce poop odor? Feed your ferret a high-quality ferret food that is primarily composed of animal protein (at least 30-40%) and low in fiber (less than 3%). Avoid foods that are high in sugars and carbohydrates, as these can contribute to digestive upset and increased fecal odor. Can I use scented litter to mask the smell of ferret poop? It’s generally best to avoid scented litters, as the added fragrance can be irritating to ferrets and may not effectively mask the odor. Instead, focus on choosing an absorbent, odor-controlling litter and cleaning the litter box frequently. How often should I bathe my ferret? Over-bathing can strip a ferret’s skin of its natural oils, leading to increased oil production and muskier odor. Bathe your ferret only when necessary, using a ferret-specific shampoo or a mild, unscented baby shampoo, no more than once a month unless directed otherwise by a vet. Are there any health conditions that can cause increased ferret poop odor? Yes, certain medical conditions, such as intestinal parasites, digestive disorders, or infections, can contribute to increased fecal odor. If you notice a significant change in your ferret’s poop consistency or smell, consult a veterinarian. How do I clean my ferret’s cage to reduce odor? Regularly clean the entire ferret cage, including bedding, toys, and food dishes. Wash all washable items with hot, soapy water. Wipe down the cage surfaces with a ferret-safe cleaner. Is it normal for ferret poop to have a strong odor? Yes, it’s normal for ferret poop to have a distinctive odor, as they are carnivores. However, the intensity of the odor can be managed through proper diet, hygiene, and health care. Does the ferret’s sex influence poop odor? While male ferrets tend to have a stronger muskier body odor overall, the sex of the ferret doesn’t directly impact the smell of their feces. The primary factors influencing poop odor are diet, hygiene, and health. Can I train my ferret to use a litter box? Yes, ferrets are intelligent animals and can be trained to use a litter box. Consistent training and placement of the litter box in a preferred elimination area can help establish good litter box habits. They tend to relieve themselves in corners so that is a good place to start. What should I do if my ferret has diarrhea? Diarrhea in ferrets can be caused by a variety of factors, including dietary changes, stress, infections, or parasites. If your ferret has diarrhea, consult a veterinarian to determine the underlying cause and receive appropriate treatment. Do not self-treat! Are there any natural remedies to reduce ferret poop odor? While there are no guaranteed “natural remedies” to eliminate ferret poop odor entirely, some owners have found that adding a small amount of plain yogurt (with live cultures) to their ferret’s diet can help improve digestion and potentially reduce odor. However, always consult with a veterinarian before making any significant dietary changes. The best natural remedy is consistent cleaning and appropriate food. Managing Does ferret poop smell? is best approached through consistent, proper care.

title: Hanshow Unveils Nebular Lux at NRF 2026 Europe, Advancing More Responsive and Low Carbon Shelf-Edge Infrastructure
description: New-generation ESL harvests ambient indoor light to support more responsive shelf-edge operations, reducing daily energy consumption by up to 46% under a representative retail operating scenario. PARIS, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hanshow today unveiled Ne…
content: New-generation ESL harvests ambient indoor light to support more responsive shelf-edge operations, reducing daily energy consumption by up to 46% under a representative retail operating scenario. PARIS, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hanshow today unveiled Nebular Lux, its new-generation electronic shelf label (ESL), at NRF 2026: Retail's Big Show Europe. Built on a hybrid energy architecture, Nebular Lux harvests ambient indoor light to supplement battery power, bringing together greater operational responsiveness and lower battery-related carbon impact at the shelf edge. Under a representative retail operating scenario, Nebular Lux reduces daily energy consumption by approximately 46% compared with conventional ESL deployments. Across a deployment of one million labels, the solution can help avoid approximately 202 metric tons of CO₂ emissions associated with battery production and replacement activities over a 10-year operating period. Together, these efficiencies demonstrate how a more energy-efficient shelf-edge architecture can support both long-term operational performance and sustainability at scale. As retailers deploy millions of electronic shelf labels, the shelf edge is becoming an increasingly important part of day-to-day store operations. At the same time, retailers need to support more frequent and responsive shelf-edge services without compromising the long operational life required at scale. Balancing responsiveness, longevity and sustainability is therefore becoming an increasingly important consideration as digital shelf infrastructure evolves. Nebular Lux is designed to address this challenge through a hybrid energy architecture that combines ambient indoor light harvesting, ultra-low-power electronics, and Hanshow's fifth-generation communication protocol HiLPC, reflecting system-level engineering across energy management, communications, positioning and retail-scale product integration. This expanded energy budget supports more frequent positioning and longer-duration LED signalling, helping retailers scale high-frequency use cases such as picking, replenishment, product finding and location-based services without compromising standard product longevity. For retailers, this can translate into better product availability, greater operational efficiency and more responsive store execution. At the same time, lower battery consumption and fewer replacement requirements can help reduce lifecycle operating costs, improve total cost of ownership and strengthen the return on ESL infrastructure investments. "The next generation of shelf infrastructure needs to do more than remain connected — it needs to become more responsive while also using energy more intelligently," said Philippe Brochard, Chairman of the Advisory Board at Hanshow. "Nebular Lux brings these two priorities together, helping retailers create a faster connection between insight and action while supporting a more sustainable foundation for Store Digital Twin at scale." Nebular Lux demonstrates how the evolution of digital shelf infrastructure can support both more responsive store operations and longer-term sustainability goals. At NRF 2026: Retail's Big Show Europe, Hanshow is demonstrating how Nebular Lux integrates with its broader Store Digital Twin portfolio at Hall 6, Booth E-020. Hanshow's intelligent robotics solution NexMate is also making its European debut at the event, further expanding Store Digital Twin with intelligent sensing and execution capabilities.

title: TikTok founder Zhang Yiming overtakes Gautam Adani as Asia’s richest
description: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming now leads Asia's wealthiest individuals. His fortune has surpassed Gautam Adani's due to the booming artificial intelligence sector. Zhang's wealth has significantly increased, driven by ByteDance's AI ventures and TikTok's glob…
content: Listen to this article in summarized format Zhang, 43, has seen his wealth rise more than eightfold from the $13 billion Bloomberg recorded in March 2019. His fortune jumped by more than $12 billion this month after the news agency analysed updated valuations reported by investment firms including BlackRock, Fidelity Investments and T. Rowe Price. Also Read: TikTok billionaire overtakes Mukesh Ambani as Asia’s second-richest person The latest ranking puts Zhang ahead of Adani on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Adani’s wealth had climbed as high as $120 billion in June but has declined in recent months amid a rebalancing of stocks within the MSCI index and a broader selloff linked to higher oil prices and bond yields, Bloomberg reported. How Zhang’s wealth surged Zhang built his fortune through ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, which has grown into one of the world’s biggest social media platforms. The company has also expanded aggressively into artificial intelligence, with products including the Doubao chatbot and Seedance video-generation tool. AI boom is creating fortunes that are beginning to overtake those built around more traditional industries, including Adani’s energy-to-retail empire and Mukesh Ambani’s conglomerate. AI-related products and services now represent ByteDance’s biggest opportunity beyond its video platform, although competition in China's AI market remains a major risk, Su said. From TikTok to AI Zhang’s rise in wealth comes after years of regulatory and geopolitical uncertainty surrounding TikTok, particularly in the US. ByteDance transferred parts of TikTok’s US operations to American investors earlier this year, helping the company move beyond a period of uncertainty over the app’s future in the country, the report showed. The Bloomberg Billionaires Index applies a 10% risk discount to ByteDance because the company is privately held. Zhang was already China's richest person, driven by TikTok’s global reach and ByteDance’s growing AI business. His latest ascent reflects the broader shift in Asia’s billionaire rankings as AI-related businesses generate new wealth. China has also continued to push investment in artificial intelligence as it competes with the US for influence in advanced technology.

title: Sensex, Nifty hold morning gains at midday; IT drags as metals, FMCG shine ahead of Fed call
description: Equity benchmarks were holding onto moderate gains at midday on Wednesday, though the rally remained selective and uneven, with information technology stocks emerging as the session’s key drag while metals, FMCG and insurance counters lent support.
content: Equity benchmarks were holding onto moderate gains at midday on Wednesday, though the rally remained selective and uneven, with information technology stocks emerging as the session’s key drag while metals, FMCG and insurance counters lent support. At 12.46 PM, the BSE Sensex was trading at 74,371.81, up 367.99 points or 0.50 per cent from its previous close of 74,003.82. The NSE Nifty 50 stood at 23,247.35, up 128.75 points or 0.56 per cent from its previous close of 23,118.60. Both indices had opened positively, the Sensex at 74,249.31 and the Nifty at 23,201.60, and were broadly sustaining those levels into the afternoon session, though without any meaningful extension of gains. Broader market breadth on the BSE painted a cautious picture. Of 4,358 stocks traded, 2,331 declined against 1,791 advances, with 236 unchanged. A total of 234 stocks hit 52-week lows against just 70 at 52-week highs. Stocks in lower circuit numbered 253, compared with 125 in upper circuit, underlining the absence of a broad-based recovery. Top gainers and losers Among Nifty 50 gainers, HDFC Life Insurance led with a rise of 2.31 per cent to ₹528.00, followed by Nestlé India, up 2.26 per cent to ₹1,392.80. Tata Consumer Products gained 2.15 per cent to ₹1,007.30, ITC rose 2.05 per cent to ₹263.30, and Hindalco advanced 1.95 per cent to ₹977.40, with the metals counter benefiting from a recovery in global commodity prices. The technology sector, however, reversed its Tuesday outperformance and emerged as the session’s biggest laggard. TCS fell 1.69 per cent to ₹2,213.00, while Wipro dropped 1.61 per cent to ₹167.27. Infosys was down 1.10 per cent to ₹1,065.10, Tech Mahindra slipped 0.89 per cent to ₹1,561.90, and IndiGo declined 0.84 per cent to ₹4,736.00. On the commodities front, precious metals were recovering ahead of the Fed decision. COMEX Gold was trading near $4,370, up 1.02 per cent, while MCX Gold was up 0.56 per cent, recovering off the ₹1,50,700–₹1,50,000 support zone. COMEX Silver outperformed with a 2 per cent gain, trading above $65, while MCX Silver was up over 1 per cent near ₹2,35,000, with both metals drawing some short-covering interest. Crude consolidates, rupee under pressure Crude oil showed signs of intraday consolidation. MCX Crude Oil was pulling back 1.53 per cent, though it held above the ₹10,000 mark. WTI crude was trading near the $105–106 zone, down 0.60 per cent, with an RSI at 72 pointing to overbought conditions even as Middle East supply concerns kept a floor under prices. The rupee remained under pressure. USD/INR was trading near 95.87, just below the 96.00 resistance zone, with RSI at 63 confirming continued bullish momentum for the dollar. Reported RBI intervention through state-run banks was limiting the pace of rupee depreciation, though the currency trajectory will hinge on the Fed outcome tonight. The Nifty 50’s immediate resistance remains at 23,300–23,400, while the Bank Nifty, which opened near 56,008, faces resistance at 56,200 and a key hurdle at 56,700–56,800. Support for the Nifty is placed at 23,100–23,070, coinciding with the June low, a break below which could intensify selling pressure. With the FOMC decision due later tonight, market participants are in a holding pattern. A widely expected 25-basis-point rate hike may not move markets on its own, but Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s commentary on the inflation outlook and future rate trajectory is expected to drive volatility in currencies, bonds and equities through the remainder of the week. Published on September 16, 2026

title: Asian stocks mostly higher ahead of Fed's interest rate decision
description: Asian shares are mostly higher as investors await the Federal Reserve’s decision with high expectations of an interest rate hike
content: Wall Street holds steady ahead of the Fed's decision as oil prices, bond yields ease Wall Street is holding steady as it waits to hear from the Federal Reserve NEW YORK -- Wall Street is holding steady Wednesday as it waits to hear from the Federal Reserve, which traders expect will announce a hike to interest rates later in the day to help get the nation’s high inflation under control. The S&P 500 rose 0.4% was on track for just its second gain in the last eight days. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 34 points, or 0.1%, as of 11 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.8% higher. Stocks got help from some easing for oil prices and pressure from the bond market. The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, fell 2.5% to $106.07. had gotten to nearly $110 early this week on worries that the war with Iran will continue to clog the global flow of oil. . That helped send the yield on the 10-year Treasury, which is the centerpiece of the bond market and dictates where rates for mortgages and other loans go, down to 4.95% from 5.00% late Tuesday. Earlier this week was the first time since 2023 that the 10-year yield topped 5%. Even with Wednesday’s easing, the pressure remains high. Brent oil is still well above its $72 price from before the war with Iran, when the 10-year yield was at just 3.97%. Worries are so strong about inflation staying high that Wall Street sees it as a near certainty that Fed officials will announce their first hike to interest rates since 2023 later in the day. That’s the typical move for the Fed to combat inflation, and it works by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money, which slows the overall economy and hopefully removes fuel for prices to rise further. It also tends to undercut prices for stocks and other investments, though President Donald Trump has been lobbying for lower interest rates instead of higher. Inflation is a worldwide problem, and the European Central Bank hiked rates across the Atlantic last week to help diminish it. Traders are still betting on a slight chance the Fed may hold off on raising rates. If it does, the market could swing because investors may see it as a sign that the Fed is less committed to getting inflation lower. Fed officials will also release forecasts for where they see interest rates heading in upcoming years, providing another opportunity to inject uncertainty into the market. A report on Wednesday morning showing that shoppers spent much more at U.S. retailers last month than economists expected could embolden the Fed. It could offer a signal that the economy remains strong enough to withstand higher rates. On Wall Street, stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry held steadier following their worldwide slide earlier in the week, after leaders of the AI industry called for a slowdown in development to address safety issues for humanity. Nvidia rose 1.6%, and Advanced Micro Devices climbed 3.7%. They helped offset a drop of 13.1% for J.B. Hunt Transport Services. Its chief financial officer told a conference of analysts late Tuesday that it’s facing higher costs and expects its earnings to drop 5% to 10% from the second quarter to the third. In stock markets abroad, indexes rose across much of Europe and Asia. South Korea’s Kospi climbed 1.4% for one of the world’s biggest gains. ___ AP Business Writers Chan Ho-him and Michelle Chapman contributed to this report.

title: Andy Burnham 'to meet Donald Trump in New York next week' as tensions rise with US over Iran war, Ukraine, Falklands and AI
description: The PM is expected to hold face-to-face talks with the US president as they attend the UN General Assembly.
content: - See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source Andy Burnham is poised to meet Donald Trump for the first time as he visits New York next week. The PM is expected to hold face-to-face talks with the US president as they attend the UN General Assembly. Mr Burnham has suggested he will use the trip to lobby Mr Trump to give more support to Ukraine, and shrugged off concerns about his previous jibes at the Republican. But the encounter will be a diplomatic minefield with Transatlantic tensions running high over issues such as the Middle East crisis, Russia, Falklands, Irish unification and regulation of tech firms. Earlier this week Mr Trump described the Labour premier as a 'very nice guy' but 'on the liberal side'. He also caused a storm by seemingly backing a merger between Northern Ireland and the Republic - something that was flatly rejected by the UK Government. Andy Burnham is poised to meet Donald Trump for the first time as he visits New York next week Earlier this week Mr Trump described the Labour premier as a 'very nice guy' but on 'on the liberal side' In recent weeks the president has hinted he would not support Britain if Argentina tried to claim the Falkland Islands again. He linked the dispute to the UK's reluctance to get involved in the US-Israeli war against Iran, which has caused chaos in global energy supplies. There are reports that US officials have privately complained about the Government's online safety legislation and the prospect of under-16s being banned from social media. The UK and America have also taken different positions on AI development, with Mr Trump dismissing the need for 'guardrails' apart from having a 'very high IQ' president. Keir Starmer's initial meeting with Mr Trump was seen as an unexpected success, although relations later soured over his refusal to participate in the Iran war. Downing Street sources said Mr Burnham's meetings in New York were not yet finalised. As Manchester Mayor Mr Burnham insisted he would not give the American politician 'the time of day', and suggested he would snub a meeting. Last month Mr Burnham insisted Mr Trump had 'said things as well'. 'Everyone says things as politicians. In the moment you meet people where they're at, and you find a connection with people, and that's always been my style,' he added. 'I've had a habit of saying what I feel over the years and I'll continue to do that. 'But, at the same time, I am somebody who works with people, tries to find common ground, and obviously that's what I should be doing in this job in the British public's interest, and I will always take that approach. 'So, I'm looking forward actually to my first meeting. We had a good phone call on my first day in office and looking forward to meeting in person.'

title: Oil slips on US stock build, Mideast disruptions in focus
description: Oil prices fell today, retreating after a two-day rally following an unexpectedly large build in US crude inventories, while supply disruptions in the Middle East lingered.
content: Oil prices fell today as reports that Saudi Arabia was offering additional crude cargoes via Oman eased concerns about the scale of Middle East supply disruptions, while European diesel prices hovered near a record high. Brent crude futures were down $1.30, or 1.2%, at $107.45 a barrel this afternoon. US West Texas Intermediate futures were down $1.96, or 1.85%, at $103.87. Oil prices had gained more than $3 in the previous session after shipping industry sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh had cancelled some cargo deliveries to European customers, deepening concerns that disruptions to a critical export route could persist for weeks. However, Saudi Arabia is offering more loadings of crude oil to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfer off Oman's Sohar port after drone attacks damaged its oil pipeline to the Red Sea, people familiar with the matter said. "News around Saudi Arabia exporting from the Gulf suggests concerns that the disruption could be larger are easing," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo. Visible vessel passage through the Strait of Hormuz remained in the single digits at four yesterday, down from seven a day earlier, preliminary shipping data showed today. That was well below the 10-day average of 18. The waterway handled a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supply before the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February. Macquarie analysts said flows of crude, condensate and refined products through the Strait of Hormuz had remained resilient despite escalating hostilities in the region and may have risen to more than 7.5 million barrels per day since fighting resumed on August 30. They said the link between developments in the strait and oil flows had weakened. Citi expects near-term escalation in the Middle East to continue supporting crude oil and refined fuel prices before the Strait of Hormuz eventually reopens in the fourth quarter of 2026 with support from regional diplomatic efforts, the bank said in a note. Diesel tightness persists European gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel prices, rose to their highest intraday level since April yesterday before settling at a record high, underscoring tightness in fuel markets, though they also eased today. "Diesel's strength reflects a product-specific shortage layered on top of expensive crude," said Frank Walbaum, market analyst at Naga.com. "Europe has lost substantial diesel and jet fuel supply from the Middle East, while ongoing tensions in Eastern Europe have disrupted output at several major Russian refineries and prompted Moscow to restrict fuel exports," he said. Last week, the US national average price of diesel surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time ever. The Russian government has decided to extend restrictions on diesel exports for fuel producers until the end of October, Vedomosti daily reported last night, citing two unidentified sources. "I would expect, unless there is a peace deal or an improvement in the situation in Russia, that diesel prices stay supported," sais Staunovo at UBS. Meanwhile, US crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories all rose last week, market sources said yesterday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude inventories rose by 7.1 million barrels in the week ended September 11, the sources said, citing API data. That compared with analyst expectations for a draw of about 1.6 million barrels, a Reuters poll showed.

title: Eating grass, meditation and more – What Tuchel said in viral documentary
description: The FA have released a documentary called Reflections: England's World Cup Journey; Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel looks back on the summer campaign and explains how it has bonded him and the group for the upcoming Nations League and Euro 2028 challenges
content: Thomas Tuchel: England boss on World Cup reflections, wishing he'd eaten Azteca grass and an 'exciting' future The FA have released a documentary called Reflections: England's World Cup Journey; Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel looks back on the summer campaign and explains how it has bonded him and the group for the upcoming Nations League and Euro 2028 challenges Wednesday 16 September 2026 09:20, UK Thomas Tuchel wishes he'd eaten grass from the Azteca pitch after England's World Cup win over Mexico this summer. That's just one of the statements from the England boss which has drawn attention across social media, following the FA releasing a new documentary called 'Reflections: England's World Cup Journey'. In the documentary, Tuchel sits alongside former England international and Sky Sports pundit Daniel Sturridge to look back on England's campaign, which ultimately saw the team finish third, having lost in the semi-finals to Argentina. England's standout performance of the tournament came in the last-16 win over Mexico in Mexico City, where they played for over 35 minutes with 10 men but prevailed 3-2. "I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote, 'I regret that I didn't eat some grass after the match to keep something from this in my body forever'," said Tuchel. On the unity his players showed in that match, Tuchel pointed to their reaction to Jordan Henderson falling and breaking his arm in the post-match celebrations. "If you needed any proof, any proof for what it meant to these players and how they were with each other, it was the moment when Jordan fell over and broke his arm," said Tuchel. "Within a second, the players were there, every single player was there, stopping the celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan and not going nowhere in full empathy. It was just so special." The film will be released on Wednesday September 16 exclusively on the England app. The build-up to the Mexico game had been dominated by talk of the altitude of the Azteca stadium but also the potential for weather delays, which proved founded with kick-off pushed back. But Tuchel says a calm came over the group when they trained together in Mexico before the match and meditation and manifestation helped them to achieve the victory. "In the middle of Mexico City and we arrived and it's an oasis, it's so peaceful, it's an unbelievable pitch and it is so calm, it is so peaceful that it did something to the players," said Tuchel. "They came out from the gym straight out on the pitch, they were having phone calls, walking around, it was such a peaceful energy. "So we came up with this line of 'silence is powerful', that we enjoy the silence, we're in a home country, we will play against the whole nation, the whole nation will be against us, the stadium, it's almost impossible to win in the stadium, no one has ever done it before in a World Cup match. "So let's enjoy the silence, the power of the silence. We even had five minutes on the match day of meditation and manifestation of the last whistle." The FA are currently undergoing a review of England's World Cup campaign but Tuchel says the experience has bonded him and the group together and he is "excited" about what comes next. England face world champions Spain in the Nations League in the upcoming international break with the 2028 Euros the next major tournament. Tuchel reckons preparing for that tournament will be easier than the planning which was required for the 2026 World Cup. "It created a huge bond to these players, it feels like they are my players now. This is the beauty of it," said Tuchel. "When you have a manager and then you have success and you have painful moments together, but you have so much time together and then you create a natural bond. "I'm happy to see them, I'm happy to challenge them, happy to push them and very proud to be a part of them. "I'm very excited. I'm excited to work with these players. I'm excited to have new, young players that we can bring into camp and that they can learn. "We've got another step closer and I think we're there. "It's very difficult to prepare a World Cup in the US, but it's possible to prepare for a Euros and be prepared in Nations League tier one. "The target is to have another 10 matches. We had 10 matches in the US, eight wins, one draw, one painful loss, but that is something to build on. "We have all the right to hold our heads high and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges. "We have four matches in the Nations League coming up and that's where the focus is." Tuchel on Harry Kane going to another level "Just so easy. He's always there, he's always in training, he always wants to train. The level to which he got himself now, since he's at Bayern Munich. "The level of commitment and training, how he arrived in prep camp, how he arrived in the qualification matches, the speech after the October camp, and he straight away stood up in the dressing room and said, 'guys, we will keep on going in November, this is what we do'. "He found another level in his game, but also as a personality, and how he shows up for training, how he drives training standards is one of a kind. The finishing is out of control good." On Jude Bellingham living up to his full potential "He was one of the players of the tournament, not only for us, but of the whole tournament. "He lived up to his full potential, you could just see what a competitor, what a machine he is, and he just thrives on the pressure. He just loves these moments, he loves these stages, it brings out the very best. "He came with an amazing mindset into camp, with the best physical preparation. He came fresh, he came hungry, hungry for football, hungry for minutes into camp. He took his place and decided every single match for us." On the England fans and their 'special' connection with the team "They lived up to the high expectations. "Everyone told me, 'wait until the tournament starts, we will have the best fans, we will be right on top, it will be amazing, the amount of people…' and it was just like that from the first moment. "They just felt this team. I believe that fans have a sense, maybe they cannot name it, someone will say, 'yeah, they give everything, they're sweating, after the whistle goes, they have to sit down because they're so tired'. For everyone it's maybe different, they feel it, they could sense it, that this team is together and this team means it. "That's what made the connection so strong. That was not artificial. That was very special."

title: GameChange Energy completes commissioning of its Genius Tracker™ for the landmark Mooi Plaats Solar PV project
description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GameChange Energy, a global provider of renewable energy infrastructure solutions, announced the completion of its Genius Tracker™ 1P system for the 283 MWp Mooi Plaats Solar PV Plant in South Africa, on…
content: CAPE TOWN, South Africa, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GameChange Energy, a global provider of renewable energy infrastructure solutions, announced the completion of its Genius Tracker™ 1P system for the 283 MWp Mooi Plaats Solar PV Plant in South Africa, one of the country's largest single-site solar power projects. The project forms part of the Koruson 2 renewable energy cluster and was developed and constructed by Envusa Energy, the renewable energy joint venture between EDF Power Solutions and Anglo American, with CEEC/CGGC serving as EPC contractor. Located near Noupoort in the Northern Cape, the Mooi Plaats Solar PV Plant will supply renewable electricity to Anglo American's mining operations in South Africa, including Kumba Iron Ore and De Beers as well as Valterra Platinum, supporting long-term decarbonisation and energy resilience objectives across the mining sector. "The Northern Cape region presents harsh environmental and site conditions, including high wind exposure, elevated temperatures, dusty conditions, and demanding construction environments that place significant demands on tracker design and execution. Our Genius Tracker™ 1P system was selected to support reliable performance under these conditions while enabling efficient installation across a project of this scale. We appreciate the strong collaboration with CGGC, Envusa Energy, and the broader project team throughout execution of this important development," said Vikas Bansal, CEO – International at GameChange Energy. The project is expected to generate nearly 360 million kWh of renewable electricity annually while contributing to long-term reductions in Scope 2 emissions associated with mining operations. During construction, the project supported more than 1,600 jobs and included approximately R20 million in socio-economic development investment for surrounding communities. "Mooi Plaats Solar PV Plant is a significant renewable energy infrastructure project both in terms of scale and execution complexity. Delivery of a project of this nature requires coordination across multiple stakeholders, technologies, and construction activities, and we appreciate the partnership with GameChange Energy throughout the tracker installation phase," said Hanli Smit, Head of Execution, Envusa Energy. About GameChange Energy GameChange Energy is a global energy infrastructure company delivering integrated, highly engineered solutions for utility-scale renewable energy and critical power applications. Through our portfolio of operating companies, we provide solar trackers, fixed-tilt mounting systems, eBOS solutions, transformers, drone-based asset monitoring, and customized infrastructure solutions for renewable energy plants, data centers, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). Our technologies are designed to reduce risk, improve performance, and deliver reliable operation worldwide. GameChange Energy is engineering the future of clean energy infrastructure. For more information about GameChange Energy, visit: www.gamechangeenergy.com Media Contact Nisha Wadhwani Lead – Marketing, GameChange Energy SOURCE GameChange Energy
