title: How long will birds sit on unfertilized eggs?
description: How Long Will Birds Sit on Unfertilized Eggs?: Understanding Incubation Instincts A bird’s dedication to incubation is powerful, but even the strongest instinct has its limits. Generally, most birds will abandon an unfertilized egg after the typical incubatio…
content: A bird’s dedication to incubation is powerful, but even the strongest instinct has its limits. Generally, most birds will abandon an unfertilized egg after the typical incubation period has passed or shortly thereafter, ranging from a few days to a couple of weeks depending on the species. Incubation is a crucial and fascinating aspect of avian reproduction. It involves consistent warmth and protection provided by the parent bird to develop embryos within eggs. However, what happens when an egg is not fertilized? How long will birds sit on unfertilized eggs? The answer to this question depends on several factors, including the bird species, the strength of the incubation instinct, and environmental cues. The incubation instinct is a deeply ingrained behavior driven by hormones and triggered by the presence of eggs in a nest. This instinct compels birds to: - Maintain a specific nest temperature - Turn eggs regularly for even development - Protect the nest from predators - Even brood eggs that are not theirs This powerful drive ensures the survival of the next generation. The intensity and duration of this instinct vary significantly between species and even individual birds. While birds may possess impressive instincts, they cannot visually determine if an egg is fertilized early in the incubation process. Some birds may be able to detect differences in weight or subtle changes within the egg through careful observation, but the determination of fertilization status takes time. How long will birds sit on unfertilized eggs? The answer depends heavily on the typical incubation period for that particular bird species. Birds typically incubate eggs until they hatch. After the normal incubation period is over, birds will remain vigilant, giving the eggs some additional time to hatch. After that period has passed, the bird will usually give up on the eggs and start nesting elsewhere, or focus their attention on food. External factors also influence incubation behavior. For example: - Food Availability: If food becomes scarce, a bird might abandon unfertilized eggs sooner to prioritize its own survival. - Predator Pressure: Constant threats can disrupt incubation and lead to nest abandonment. - Weather Conditions: Extreme weather can endanger both the parent bird and the eggs, potentially shortening the incubation period. Several factors can result in unfertilized eggs: - Inexperienced Mates: Young birds might not be successful at mating. - Infertility: Older birds or those with health problems may have reduced fertility. - Mating Problems: Physical incompatibilities or behavioral issues can prevent successful fertilization. - Environmental Factors: Pollution or toxins can affect fertility. While the instinct to incubate is strong, prolonged incubation of unfertilized eggs can have negative consequences: - Energy Depletion: The bird expends valuable energy on a futile effort, potentially weakening its overall health. - Missed Breeding Opportunities: Prolonged incubation can delay or prevent a second breeding attempt in the same season. - Increased Risk of Predation: Spending excessive time at the nest increases the risk of the parent bird being attacked. How can I tell if an egg is unfertilized without disturbing the nest? It’s difficult to know for sure without candling (shining a bright light through the egg), which is best left to experienced bird handlers to avoid disturbance. However, if the typical incubation period has passed and there’s still no sign of hatching, it’s a strong indication the egg is unfertilized. Observe from a distance to avoid disturbing the bird further. What should I do if I find a nest with abandoned unfertilized eggs? In most cases, it’s best to leave the nest undisturbed. Nature will take its course. Removing the eggs could encourage the birds to rebuild a new nest, leading to more energy expenditure. However, if the nest poses a hazard, consult with a local wildlife rehabilitation center. Does replacing unfertilized eggs with fertile ones help the situation? Generally, it is not recommended to interfere with a bird’s nest by replacing eggs. This can disrupt the natural process and potentially introduce diseases or behavioral problems. Furthermore, moving eggs is illegal in many places. Will a bird lay more eggs if its first clutch is unfertilized? Yes, many bird species will lay a second or even third clutch if their first nesting attempt fails. This is especially common in migratory birds with short breeding seasons. This depends on food supply and weather conditions, however. What is “candling” and how is it used to determine egg fertility? Candling involves shining a bright light through an eggshell in a darkened room. A fertilized egg will typically show visible veins and a developing embryo. An unfertilized egg will appear clear or uniformly colored without signs of development. This is a delicate process best performed by experienced individuals. Are some bird species more prone to laying unfertilized eggs than others? Yes, factors like age, health, and genetic compatibility can influence fertility. Some species may also be more susceptible to environmental toxins that affect reproductive success. Do male birds play a role in determining egg fertility? Yes, the male bird’s fertility is just as important as the female’s. Infertile males will naturally result in unfertilized eggs. How does diet affect a bird’s ability to lay fertilized eggs? A proper diet rich in calcium, protein, and vitamins is essential for egg production and fertility. Nutritional deficiencies can lead to weaker eggs or reduced fertility. What happens to the unfertilized eggs after the bird abandons the nest? In most cases, the eggs will decompose naturally. Scavengers may also consume them. Over time, the eggshells will break down and become part of the environment. Is it possible for an egg to appear fertile but still not hatch? Yes, there are instances of early embryonic death. The egg might appear to be developing initially, but for various reasons, the embryo stops growing before hatching. Can environmental pollutants affect egg fertility? Absolutely. Exposure to pesticides, heavy metals, and other pollutants can negatively impact a bird’s reproductive system and reduce egg fertility. It’s vital to protect habitats from pollution to ensure healthy bird populations. Does the age of a bird influence the likelihood of unfertilized eggs? Yes, very young or very old birds are more likely to lay unfertilized eggs or eggs with thin shells. Prime breeding age typically corresponds with optimal fertility.

title: Nifty FMCG up 2% as festive season puts consumer stocks in spotlight
description: In the Nifty FMCG basket 13 stocks advanced while only 2 declined. Intraday, the FMCG index was up 1.82 per cent to 45,645.20.
content: ITC leads as Nifty FMCG gains 2%; festive season puts sector in focus In the Nifty FMCG basket 13 stocks advanced while only 2 declined. Intraday, the FMCG index was up 1.82 per cent to 45,645.20. Listen to This Article Shares of fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies snapped a four-day losing streak to gain over 1 per cent on Wednesday with most frontline stocks Hindustan Unilever (HUL), ITC, Dabur India, Emami, Godrej Consumer Products and Procter & Gamble Hygiene and Health Care gaining in the range of 2 to 4 per cent. In the Nifty FMCG basket 13 stocks advanced while only 2 declined. At 11:47 AM, the index was up 1.68 per cent at 45,583.90, compared to a 0.46 per cent gain in the Nifty 50. In intraday trading, the FMCG index was up 1.82 per cent to 45,645.20. Sunny Agrawal, deputy vice president, fundamental research, SBI Securities noted that the positive reaction to the Nifty FMCG index or FMCG companies today is due to current uncertain environment, “money is rotating out of riskier sectors and shifting to defensives like FMCG,” he said. Agrawal also attributed the surge to the onsent of the festive season that has begun with Ganesh Chaturthi. “Usually, the festive season extends till Diwali and Christmas in the month of December. So, it is expected that the September quarter and December quarter should be relatively better in terms of the demand environment, and that is something that should support FMCG as a sector.” The Nifty FMCG index snapped a four-session losing streak on Wednesday after falling 1.06 per cent over the previous four sessions. The index gained 1.82 per cent in intraday trade. Vipin Kumar, AVP research at Globe Capital Market noted that the Nifty FMCG index is exhibiting a lower-high and lower-low structure, trading below its key short-term as well as long-term moving averages. “Elevated crude oil prices have a direct negative impact on inflation, which presents a significant headwind for the FMCG industry. Considering the current chart structure, the possibility of a bounce-back or relief rally cannot be ruled out at this juncture; however, any recovery up to the 47,500–48,000 spot levels is likely to attract selling interest,” he said. Also Read Disclaimer: View and outlook shared belong to the respective brokerages/analysts and are not endorsed by Business Standard. Readers discretion is advised. title: Iraola reveals what pleased him most about Liverpool win over Spurs
description: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola took satisfaction from his side’s energy levels more than anything else after beating Spurs in the League Cup on Tuesday evening. Alexis Mac Allister gave the Reds the l...
content: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola took satisfaction from his side’s energy levels more than anything else after beating Spurs in the League Cup on Tuesday evening. Alexis Mac Allister gave the Reds the lead at Anfield with a beautiful finish before Cody Gakpo marked his return from injury with a powerful strike. Conor Gallagher pulled one back for Tottenham midway through the second half, but Dominik Szoboszlai completed a 3-1 victory with an exceptional half-volley in the 90th minute. The win, which puts Liverpool into the hat for the fourth round draw, came just days after they put in a rather lethargic display against Fulham at the weekend that resulted in a goalless draw. Iraola reveals what pleased him most about Liverpool win over Spurs “I am pleased with the performance,” Iraola told BBC Radio 5 Live. “I think there have been different phases in the game but overall I liked the energy. We scored but I am happy because we are in the next round. “I think at 2-0, they have to take a risk and win some territory. We were defending well but conceding a lot of set-pieces and when they scored that put us under some pressure. Luckily for us we found a way to score a third and finish the game properly.” On Szoboszlai’s wonder goal, Iraola added: “I think the thing with Dom is when he is going to shoot he has a chance to score. With him you believe because he has done it before. He is a great finisher.” Andy Robertson received applause from the Liverpool fans when he came off the bench shortly after Gakpo’s goal for his first appearance at Anfield since joining Spurs on a free transfer in the summer. “I think he deserves all this and I was happy,” Iraola said. “I was thinking he honestly deserves this because he has given so much to Liverpool.” Read More – Five of the best Premier League away kits in 2026/27 See Also – The four clubs making their Champions League debut this season

title: Liverpool’s Young Guns Impress as Tottenham Are Beaten at Anfield
description: Liverpool 3–1 Tottenham – EFL Cup Post-Match ReportBy Steven SmithLiverpool returned to winning ways at Anfield with a deserved 3–1 victory over Tottenham in the fourth round of the EFL Cup, wit...
content: Liverpool 3–1 Tottenham – EFL Cup Post-Match Report By Steven Smith Liverpool returned to winning ways at Anfield with a deserved 3–1 victory over Tottenham in the fourth round of the EFL Cup, with Andoni Iraola making several changes and handing opportunities to several younger players. some frustration of a draw with Fulham, a reaction was required and the Reds provided one. This was not a perfect performance, with Tottenham enjoying 56 per cent possession and registering 17 shots compared with Liverpool’s 12, but there was considerably more energy, purpose and determination from Iraola’s side. Most importantly, several players given an opportunity showed exactly why competition for places needs to be increased. 🏴💥 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗬 𝗡𝗬𝗢𝗡𝗜 (𝟭𝟵, 𝗖𝗠) vs Tottenham: • 62 Minutes Played • 6 Ball Recoveries • 3/4 Ground Duels Won • 100% Aerial Duels Won • 3 Tackles • 6 Ball Recoveries • 100% Successful Long Balls, 2/2 • 95% Pass Accuracy UNDERRATED GEM 💎 pic.twitter.com/hojdiNpnwU — Rising Stars XI (@RisingStarXI) September 15, 2026 The Starting Eleven Liverpool XI GK – Giorgi Mamardashvili RB – Jeremie Frimpong CB – Joe Gomez (c) CB – Ronald Araújo LB – Milos Kerkez CM – Alexis Mac Allister CM – Trey Nyoni CM – James McConnell RW – Rio Ngumoha LW – Cody Gakpo CF – Lewis Koumas Substitutes Used Jérémy Jacquet → Joe Gomez (45’) Ryan Gravenberch → Trey Nyoni (62’) Dominik Szoboszlai → James McConnell (62’) Bradley Barcola → Rio Ngumoha (72’) Alexander Isak → Lewis Koumas (86’) Goals Liverpool 1–0 Tottenham – Alexis Mac Allister – 21’ Liverpool 2–0 Tottenham – Cody Gakpo (Alexis Mac Allister) – 54’ Liverpool 2–1 Tottenham – Conor Gallagher (Mateus Fernandes) – 69’ Liverpool 3–1 Tottenham – Dominik Szoboszlai (Cody Gakpo) – 90+1’ Match Statistics Possession – Liverpool 44% | Tottenham 56% Total Shots – Liverpool 12 | Tottenham 17 Shots on Target – Liverpool 5 | Tottenham 6 Fouls – Liverpool 15 | Tottenham 11 Corners – Liverpool 5 | Tottenham 9 First Half The first half was a much more encouraging response from Liverpool following the disappointment against Fulham. Iraola made significant changes, with Joe Gomez captaining a side containing Trey Nyoni, James McConnell, Lewis Koumas and Rio Ngumoha, while Cody Gakpo was moved into a wide attacking role. Tottenham started with intent and Mamardashvili was called upon early, producing an excellent save to keep the scores level. Liverpool gradually grew into the contest and found the breakthrough after 21 minutes. Alexis Mac Allister produced a superb finish, arriving at the right moment before placing the ball into the top corner. The goal gave Liverpool greater confidence, while Nyoni was increasingly influential in the deeper midfield role. That was one of the most important elements of the evening. After the problems identified against Fulham, Nyoni provided a genuine anchor in front of the defence. He looked comfortable receiving possession, moved the ball intelligently and showed the positional discipline required from somebody operating deeper. James McConnell also worked tirelessly, while Lewis Koumas provided energy and physicality across the attacking line. Liverpool went into half time ahead, and there was a sense that the changes had worked. Second Half The second half was where Liverpool took control of the contest. Cody Gakpo doubled the advantage in the 54th minute with an excellent strike from the angle after Mac Allister supplied the assist. Gakpo was outstanding throughout and looked increasingly comfortable in Iraola’s faster and more direct system. Tottenham refused to disappear, however, and Conor Gallagher pulled one back in the 69th minute after Mateus Fernandes created the opportunity. The visitors had more possession and continued to threaten, but Liverpool remained dangerous on the counter. Iraola began refreshing his side, bringing on Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai in the 62nd minute before Bradley Barcola and eventually Alexander Isak entered the contest. Szoboszlai initially should have put the game beyond Tottenham before making amends in stoppage time. Gakpo was again involved, providing the assist for the Hungarian’s thunderous 90+1-minute finish. That sealed the victory. Mamardashvili deserves considerable credit for his contribution too. The Georgian produced another outstanding save after the restart, going low to his left before later making an extraordinary one-handed stop. His positioning for Tottenham’s goal was disappointing, but his shot-stopping was excellent. That goal was Steven Gerrard esque from Dominik Szoboszlai tonight 🚀👌 pic.twitter.com/sOLI0xPNWL — Anfield Watch (@AnfieldWatch) September 15, 2026 Final Thoughts This was a solid performance, especially given the number of changes made by Iraola. More importantly, it provided the Liverpool manager with some useful answers. Trey Nyoni showed why the discussion around a specialist defensive midfielder cannot simply be ignored. The youngster gave Liverpool greater balance from the deeper position and looked increasingly assured as the game progressed. Mac Allister was superb, Gakpo was outstanding and Mamardashvili demonstrated why Liverpool have such confidence in his ability. The younger players also took their opportunity. Koumas worked relentlessly, McConnell provided energy and Ngumoha showed flashes of the attacking ability that makes him such an exciting prospect. Liverpool still have work to do. The 17 shots conceded and the amount of possession Tottenham enjoyed demonstrate that this is not yet a finished side. But after the flat performance against Fulham, the most important thing was the reaction. Iraola changed the personnel, demanded more intensity and received it. Liverpool move into the next stage of the EFL Cup with confidence restored, while the manager has gained valuable information about the players competing for regular places. And Trey Nyoni may have just made his case for many more minutes. Steven Smith’s Pre-Match Prediction: Liverpool 2–1 Tottenham Final Score: Liverpool 3–1 Tottenham

title: Oil slips on US stock build, Middle East disruptions limit losses
description: Brent crude futures fell 73 cents, or 0.67 percent, to $108.02 a barrel at 0450 GMT
content: Oil slips on US stock build, Middle East disruptions limit losses Oil prices fell on Wednesday, retreating after a two-day rally following an unexpectedly large build in US crude inventories, while supply disruptions in the Middle East lingered. Brent crude futures fell 73 cents, or 0.67 percent, to $108.02 a barrel at 0450 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate futures were down $1.1, or 1.04 percent, at $104.73 a barrel. Both benchmarks settled more than $3 higher and at their highest levels since May 19 on Tuesday, as the Yanbu loading suspension stoked supply concerns and Saudi Arabia cut oil shipments to Europe. US crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories all rose last week, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude inventories rose by 7.1 million barrels in the week ended September 11, the sources said, citing API data. That compared with analysts' expectations for a draw of about 1.6 million barrels, according to a Reuters poll. API's data showed unexpected builds in gasoline and diesel inventories have weighed on prices, but regional stock increases do not change the underlying tightness in the global crude market, Haitong Futures said in a note. Despite the inventory pressure, prices remained resilient as traders focused on disruptions to physical supplies, said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova, in a report on Wednesday. "The bigger concern remains the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Yanbu export infrastructure, following attacks on Saudi energy facilities," she said. European diesel futures rose to a record high on Tuesday, further highlighting tightness in fuel markets as Middle East disruptions constrained crude and product flows. Sources said on Tuesday that oil loadings at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port had been suspended after the world's biggest crude exporter shut its East-West pipeline following an attack by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Friday. Saudi Arabia is offering more loadings of crude oil to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port after drone attacks damaged its key oil pipeline to the Red Sea, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday. Visible vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz remained in the single digits at four on Tuesday, down from seven a day earlier, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday, falling well short of the 10-day average of 18. The drop in traffic through the waterway that handled a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supply before the US-Israeli war on Iran started comes after attacks in the region intensified.

title: In 1854, a 16-word message from Kolkata to Bengaluru cost 10 shillings; how Bengaluru’s telegraph era lasted until 2013
description: Bengaluru joined India's electric telegraph network in 1854, transforming communication speed. A 16-word message between Calcutta and Bengaluru cost ten shillings then. This new technology connected Bengaluru to Madras, Bellary, and Bombay. Later, a line to M…
content: Today, a message can travel from Bengaluru to almost anywhere in the world in seconds. But in the mid-19th century, sending information across long distances was a far more complicated and expensive affair. In 1854, Bengaluru became part of India's expanding electric telegraph network. The city's telegraph office opened on May 23, 1854, giving residents access to a technology that could transmit messages far faster than traditional methods of communication. A 16-word message between Calcutta (now Kolkata) and Bengaluru cost 10 shillings at the time, according to a historical chronology of Bengaluru, as per multiple reports. The price reflected how new and specialised the technology was in its early years. The wires that connected Bengaluru to bigger cities Bengaluru's telegraph connection was part of a larger line running from Madras towards Bellary, passing through the city. The network was later extended towards Bombay, placing Bengaluru on a route that connected several important centres in southern and western India. The expansion was part of the rapid development of electric telegraphy across India in the 1850s. William O'Shaughnessy, who had conducted some of the earliest experiments with electric telegraphy in India, played a major role in developing the system. Work on long-distance telegraph lines accelerated in the early 1850s. By March 1854, an electric telegraph connection between Calcutta and Agra had been established, and the network continued expanding to other major cities and towns. An account of the early Indian telegraph network published in the period noted the speed with which messages could be transmitted over long distances, making the technology particularly valuable at a time when travelling between cities could take days. Bengaluru's link with Mysore came a year later The telegraph network around Bengaluru expanded quickly. In March 1855, a telegraph line connecting Bengaluru with Mysore was established and a telegraph office was opened in Mysore. The Bengaluru historical chronology records the line as being 84 miles long, with the establishment of the two offices costing over Rs 8,000. The new connection gave Bengaluru another important communication link — this time with Mysore, the capital of the princely state. By then, the city was becoming part of a much wider network in which information could move without waiting for a person or a physical document to travel between cities. From messages carried by hand to messages sent through wires Before the telegraph, communicating over long distances generally meant relying on people or physical transport to carry information. The electric telegraph changed that equation. A message could be converted into electrical signals, sent through wires and decoded at the other end For Bengaluru, this meant that information could travel along the city's growing connections to Madras, Bellary, Bombay and Mysore. The technology also arrived at a time when Bengaluru itself was changing. Railways would follow in the next decade. In 1864, the city got its first railway connection when a line between Bengaluru Cantonment and Jolarpettai opened, creating another faster link with the wider region. Together, the telegraph and railway gradually reduced the isolation of a city whose communication and transport had previously depended heavily on slower methods. The telegraph's long life in Bengaluru The technology that began with messages priced by the word eventually became an ordinary part of communication in Bengaluru. Telegrams were used for everything from urgent personal messages to business communication, particularly when a fast written message was needed. The service remained in use in the city for more than a century and a half. Telegram service was finally discontinued in 2013, bringing an end to a system that had begun in Bengaluru in the 1850s. At the time of the shutdown, multiple reports said Bengaluru had 21 telegraph offices. What began in 1854 with a costly 16-word message had thus become part of the city's communication infrastructure for generations — long before Bengaluru's present-day reputation for connecting people through phones, computers and the internet.

title: Global Market: Japan bond yields rise as inflation concerns build ahead of Fed decision
description: Japanese government bond yields extended their rise as higher oil prices and Middle East tensions fuelled inflation concerns. Longer-dated JGB yields also climbed, while investors awaited the US Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision and assessed Japan’s fi…
content: The benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield rose 0.5 basis points to 3.035%, after touching a fresh 30-year high on Tuesday. The 20-year yield climbed 4 basis points to 3.925%, while the 30-year yield also advanced 4 basis points to 4.190%. Read more: Global Market Today: Asian stocks steady as traders await Fed decision Oil Prices Add to Inflation Concerns Reuters reported that shipping industry sources said crude loadings at Yanbu had been suspended, while Saudi Arabia had cancelled some cargo deliveries to European customers. Read more: Global Market: KOSPI climbs as chip stocks lead gains before Fed outcome US Treasury Yields Keep Pressure on Global Bond Markets The rise in Japanese bond yields also came as US Treasury yields moved higher ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy announcement. The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5% overnight, reaching 5.004% after touching 5.041%, its highest level since July 2007. The Fed was scheduled to announce its policy decision at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Wednesday following its two-day meeting. Financial markets were pricing in a 25-basis-point increase in the US benchmark interest rate to a 3.75%-4% range, along with the possibility of further tightening. Japan's Fiscal Policy in Focus Domestic Japanese policy developments are also influencing the bond market. Investors are watching a planned cabinet reshuffle and whether Minoru Kiuchi will remain as minister in charge of economic revitalisation. Reuters reported that markets have been assessing Kiuchi's position for clues about the government's approach to fiscal spending. Concerns over increased government expenditure have contributed to pressure on Japanese government bonds as investors assess the country's borrowing requirements and inflation outlook. The continued rise in longer-dated JGB yields highlights the growing sensitivity of Japan's bond market to both domestic fiscal policy and global interest-rate developments. With the Federal Reserve decision due later on Wednesday and the Bank of Japan also under scrutiny over its monetary-policy direction, investors are closely watching developments in oil prices, inflation and global bond yields for signals on the path of interest rates. title: Houthis seize strategic Red Sea islands as analysts warn of impending oil crunch
description: Militant group in Yemen captured the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish, near the chokepoint of the Bab al-Mandab strait
content: Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen, Houthi militants said on Wednesday, as the Iran-backed fighters solidified their gains following a lightning advance that has extended Tehran’s reach in the Middle East war and further disrupted global oil supplies. The Iran-backed Houthis, who since last week have swept through Yemeni towns along the Red Sea coast and seized islands in the Bab el-Mandeb strait at its mouth, released battlefield video overnight of fighters seizing armoured vehicles from Saudi-backed forces. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched fresh drone and missile strikes on the main Saudi Red Sea oil port of Yanbu, and at a southern Saudi airbase at Khamis Mushait. He did not say when the strikes had taken place. Both cities were among a wide range of locations where Saudi Arabia announced alerts on Tuesday, although there were no similar announcements on Wednesday. Saudi officials and oil company Aramco did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment. READ MORE Earlier, Saree said the Houthis had also shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. No immediate evidence was presented. Saree said the Saudis had carried out as many as 450 air strikes on Yemen this week. Officials in the Saudi-backed government that controls southern Yemen have acknowledged that their forces and those of Saudi Arabia were conducting air strikes on Houthi positions, though Riyadh has not confirmed them. The Houthis have fired repeatedly into Saudi Arabia over the past week, causing alarms over cities in the south and west. An attack blamed on Iran-aligned fighters in Iraq last week also knocked out Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, the main route used to divert exports away from the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Riyadh said its air defences had shot down a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, an attack it said crossed a “red line” of threatening shrines sacred to all Muslims. Houthi spokesperson Saree denied the group had targeted Mecca, and said the Saudi reports were propaganda. The extension of the war into Yemen threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused by the six-month-old US-Israeli war on Iran, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The price of Brent crude hovered around $108 a barrel on Wednesday, close to its highest level since May. Traders say a prolonged closure of Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline could cut off as much as 4 per cent of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume, but US energy secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days. Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quietened under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and fired at southern areas in the kingdom. Violence has intensified sharply this month as the militant group pushed back forces aligned with the Saudi-backed internationally recognised Yemeni government. Saudi Arabia’s crown prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned US president Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid. The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in 2025, but halted that campaign after reaching what Trump described as a ceasefire with the group. Trump now faces a dilemma of whether to stand by and risk the Houthi advance worsening the global energy crisis, or provide more direct military support to the Saudis and risk extending the costly US intervention to another part of the Middle East. – Reuters

title: A Japanese village was drowning in 40,000 tonnes of scallop shells; then they crushed them to make stronger safety helmets for the fishermen
description: In Sarufutsu village, the burgeoning problem of scallop shell waste has taken center stage. A plastic manufacturing firm has crafted a groundbreaking material known as Shellstic using these shells. This eco-conscious innovation leads to the creation of Shellm…
content: Sarufutsu, a village on the northernmost tip of Japan's Hokkaido, is known for scallops. The village contributes to about 15% of the country's entire scallop catch, and Japan eats tens of thousands of tons of the sweet, sashimi-grade shellfish. However, what people consume is the muscle, not the shell. The shells are nothing more than waste and gather up to become a mountain that needs to be dealt with. Every year, roughly 40,000 tons of empty scallop shells pile up around the village as processing waste. When overseas export of the shells slowed after 2021, the building mounds had nowhere to go. Unlike plastic that remains lifeless on the ground, the scallop shells can leach and contaminate the soil, turning the village's signature industry into a looming environmental problem. Then, a plastic company looked at the heaps and wondered if they could become raw material for something. The birth of 'Shellstic' The idea came from the shell's original life purpose, which is to protect the animal inside from predators and the sea. Its main forming component is calcium carbonate, a hard and abundant material. Koushi Chemical Industry, which was building on bioplastic techniques from Osaka University, worked out an idea to turn the waste into construction material. The process is simple. The discarded shells are cleaned, boiled and sterilised, then crushed into a fine calcium-carbonate powder. That powder is blended with recycled plastic, leftover offcuts from manufacturing, to make a new mouldable material the company named Shellstic, a portmanteau of shell and plastic, roughly a fifth to a half shell by content. It flows into moulds and sets like ordinary plastic, but it is part seafood waste, and making it emits an estimated 36 per cent less carbon dioxide than producing the same amount of virgin plastic. A useful product The result of this process is a product called Shellmet, shell plus helmet. Designed with Tokyo agency TBWA/Hakuhodo, it does two tasks at once. The obvious one is the material: a hard hat moulded from Shellstic, protecting the fishermen whose catch produced the shells in the first place, the shell that once guarded the scallop now guarding the scallop-fisher. The second is the shape. Following biomimicry, copying nature’s engineering — the designers gave the helmet the same ribbed, fan-grooved surface a real scallop shell has, because those ridges are structural: they are how a thin shell resists crushing. A computer simulation estimated the ribbed design could reduce stress on the helmet by around 30 per cent compared with a smooth dome. Material and shape together produced the helmet that tested about 33 per cent stronger than an equivalent made of ordinary plastic. The waste product didn’t merely substitute for plastic; it beat it. Why shell wins Calcium carbonate is a reinforcing filler, from the same mineral family that makes chalk, limestone and real seashells. Blended into a plastic matrix, the hard mineral particles stiffen the mix, much as gravel stiffens cement. Nature had already done the materials science: a scallop shell is calcium carbonate arranged, over millions of years of evolution, into one of the most efficient lightweight protective structures going. Koushi’s process borrows both halves of that, the substance and, in the ribbing, the geometry. But Shellmet is a local legend that protects Sarufutsu's own fishing association and fishermen. It still will not be able to process 40,000 tons of shells. There is still a long way to go for a complete recycling loop.

title: US, Vietnam firms to sign agreements as To Lam travels to New York, documents show
description: HANOI, Sept 16 : A string of agreements is expected to be announced next week by U.S. and Vietnamese corporations involving energy, tech, aviation and financial firms as Vietnam's leader To Lam travels to New York, according to officials and two documents rev…
content: HANOI, Sept 16 : A string of agreements is expected to be announced next week by U.S. and Vietnamese corporations involving energy, tech, aviation and financial firms as Vietnam's leader To Lam travels to New York, according to officials and two documents reviewed by Reuters. Commercial agreements, many of which are expected to be non-binding, have been for months part of Vietnam's strategy to mollify Washington as the Trump administration is threatening new tariffs on the export-reliant Southeast Asian nation. One internal planning note lists 29 agreements that could be announced on September 23 in New York at a business conference to be attended by To Lam. U.S. energy firms Murphy Oil and Chevron are expected to announce agreements with state-owned Petrovietnam, while ExxonMobil is slated to announce an accord with Vietnam Refinery and Petrochemical Corporation, the country's second-largest refinery. In February the refinery signed a non-binding oil supply agreement with Chevron, but no subsequent purchase was announced. Murphy Oil is active in oil and gas explorations in Vietnam, while ExxonMobil operates the country's largest gas field which remains however untapped. The agreements are to be announced on To Lam's last day in New York before he travels to Canada for a state visit. He is expected to speak at the U.N. General Assembly on September 22 and hold meetings with several U.S. corporations, three officials said. His schedule has not yet been officially announced. His trip is also aimed at making progress on trade talks with the United States, and possibly to agree on a trade deal which has been negotiated for more than a year, two of the officials said. However, a meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump is not certain, the sources said. Trump's schedule was not yet confirmed, a White House official said on Tuesday. Vietnam's foreign ministry nor any of the companies cited in this article immediately responded to requests for comment, some out of their business hours. AVIATION, TECH The document, which may be subject to changes and does not indicate the content of the planned agreements, also lists several deals involving Vietnam's largest private airline, Vietjet, including with aviation partners and SpaceX. The company is expected to announce the leasing of as many as 22 planes from four aviation leasing companies, including 17 Boeing 737 jets and five Airbus A321neo, according to a separate document from Vietjet. The planned contract with SpaceX is for the provision of satellite internet services from Starlink to 120 Vietjet aircraft, according to the Vietjet document. The airline also plans to sign memoranda of understanding with U.S. jet engine maintenance firms, according to the documents. The provisional list also includes an unspecified agreement between Meta and Vietnam's ministry of culture, and a separate agreement between U.S. chip giant Qualcomm with Vietnamese telecom firm VNPT. Qualcomm is already active in the rollout of Vietnam's 5G network, while Meta's Facebook is the most popular social media in the Communist-ruled nation. Visa, Mastercard and Citibank are also expected to announce agreements with financial and hospitality partners in Vietnam, according to the document.

title: Headline inflation falls 3rd consecutive month to 15.39%
description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Headline inflation rate fell by 0.04 percent to 15.39 percent in August from 15.43 percent in July 2026, representing the third consecutive month decline since June. The development was driven by a further ease in the core basket to 13.…
content: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Headline inflation rate fell by 0.04 percent to 15.39 percent in August from 15.43 percent in July 2026, representing the third consecutive month decline since June. The development was driven by a further ease in the core basket to 13.29 percent in August from 14.97 percent in July. The National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, disclosed this yesterday in its Consumer Price Index, CPI, report for August 2026. NBS stated: “In August 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 15.39 percent, down from 15.43 percent in July 2026 and stood at 23.14 percent in the same month of the preceding year (August 2025). “Looking at the movement, the August 2026 Headline inflation rate showed a decrease of 0.04 percent compared to the July 2026 Headline inflation rate. “On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in August 2026 was 0.71 percent, which was 0.86 percent lower than the rate recorded in July 2026 (1.57 percent). “This means that in August 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was lower than the rate of increase in the average price level in July 2026.” Likewise, food inflation declined by 0.74 percentage points to 19.57 percent in August from 20.31 percent in July. MoM, food inflation dropped by 4.55 percentage points showing that the average prices of food items are increasing at a slower pace in August 2026. According to the Bureau, the decline in the food inflation rate was due to changes in the average prices of palm oil, carrots, pepper, onions, cassava flour, beef, yam flour, water yam, melon (egusi), fresh ginger, fresh fish, irish potatoes, wheat grain, frozen chicken, turkey meat, yam flour, among others. NBS highlighted Adamawa (38.85 percent), Zamfara (37.96 percent), and Bayelsa (36.2 percent) as states with highest food inflation in August 2026, while Borno (-4.04 percent), Jigawa (-0.23 percent) and Kebbi (3.47 percent) recorded the slowest rise in YoY food inflation. However, MoM food inflation was highest in Katsina (9.48 percent), Rivers (8.86 percent) and Osun (8.32 percent), while Taraba (-12.42 percent), Borno (-12.15 percent), and Bauchi (-8.88 percent) recorded the slowest pace.

title: Global Market: China, Hong Kong shares rise as tech stocks gain ahead of Fed decision
description: Chinese and Hong Kong equities rose on Wednesday, led by technology stocks as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision. The Shanghai Composite gained around 0.6%, while the Hang Seng and Hang Seng Tech Index also advanced. Rising Trea…
content: The Shanghai Composite was up around 0.6%, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index gained about 0.1% in morning trading. The Hang Seng Tech Index also moved higher as technology shares provided support to the broader market. Read more: Global Market Today: Asian stocks steady as traders await Fed decision According to Reuters, investors remained focused on the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and guidance on the future path of interest rates. The outcome is being closely watched across Asian markets because changes in US borrowing costs can influence capital flows, currencies and valuations for growth-oriented stocks. Read more: US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent says rising bond yields due to 'global issues' Technology Stocks in Focus Technology shares were among the key drivers of the gains in Hong Kong, helping the market recover some ground after recent weakness. The sector has remained particularly sensitive to expectations around global interest rates because higher yields can put pressure on valuations of companies whose earnings growth is expected further in the future. Fed Decision Takes Centre Stage The Fed meeting has become the central focus for global investors this week. Reuters reported that markets were preparing for a possible 25-basis-point rate increase, with investors also assessing signals from policymakers about the direction of monetary policy beyond the immediate decision. The policy outlook has gained importance as US Treasury yields have climbed and inflation concerns have remained elevated. The US 10-year Treasury yield recently moved above 5%, adding to pressure on global equity valuations. Broader Asian Market Sentiment The gains in China and Hong Kong came amid mixed trading across Asia. Investors were balancing support from technology stocks against concerns over elevated energy prices, rising bond yields and the potential impact of tighter US monetary policy. Reuters highlighted the broader pressure facing global markets from higher oil prices and rising government bond yields, both of which have increased uncertainty over the inflation and interest-rate outlook. For Chinese and Hong Kong equities, the immediate focus remained on the Fed’s decision and accompanying guidance, with investors looking for clues on how US monetary policy could shape global liquidity and demand for riskier assets in the months ahead. title: Europe faces winter gas risks as storage lags
description: Europe is approaching winter with low gas stocks as disruptions to liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies from the Gulf push up prices and slow efforts to replenish reserves.
content: Europe is approaching winter with low gas stocks as disruptions to liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies from the Gulf push up prices and slow efforts to replenish reserves. EU storage facilities were about 68 percent full on Sept. 14, according to Gas Infrastructure Europe. Qatar has largely suspended LNG shipments amid the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. “Europe is prepared for a normal winter, but it is not well insulated against a severe one,” Erisa Pasko, lead European gas analyst at Energy Aspects, told Anadolu Agency. The consultancy expects European storage to reach 69 percent of capacity by the end of October, leaving stocks near a 14-year low heading into winter. Inventories could fall to 16 percent by the end of March even under normal weather conditions. Energy Aspects does not expect Europe to run out of gas, but says prices must remain high enough to curb demand and attract LNG cargoes. Pasko also warned that gas becomes harder to withdraw quickly as storage levels decline. Germany is the most exposed major market, she said. Its storage was 55.8 percent full on Sept. 14, compared with 52.5 percent in the Netherlands. The European Commission said on Sept. 3 there was no immediate threat to gas supplies. It cited more diverse supply sources, greater LNG import capacity and lower demand as reasons the EU was better prepared than in 2021-22.

title: Gulzar suicide puts Punjab AAP govt in spot ahead of polls
description: A Dalit labourer's suicide after questioning a minister about drugs has intensified political attacks. The incident has provided opposition parties a significant issue ahead of elections. The family's petition is expected to be heard by the high court this we…
content: CHANDIGARH/NEW DELHI: The suicide of Dalit labourer Gulzar Singh after he was allegedly harassed for questioning Punjab’s finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema for ‘failing to curb drug menace’ has put AAP govt in a spot as the party is caught in a pincer attack from Congress, BJP and Akali Dal ahead of assembly elections. At a time when AAP is on an overdrive to retain its solitary govt in the country to maintain its relevance in the opposition space, the tragic incident has given its rivals a helpful handful, more so as Scheduled Castes — at nearly 32%, the highest for any state — are a crucial voting bloc in Punjab. The matter is likely to be heard by the Punjab and Haryana high court this week and the family of Gulzar Singh is among the petitioners. The Dalit labourer, distressed by his son’s addiction, had questioned Cheema, an influential figure in the AAP govt, at a public gathering about why ‘chitta’ (synthetic drug) was freely available in the village, which is part of Cheema’s constituency. In video statements he recorded before his death, Gulzar alleged that he was threatened and humiliated for confronting the minister and asked to apologise. His death, which has been taken up by National Commission for Scheduled Castes and National Human Rights Commission, has led the opposition to corner the Bhagwant Mann govt over its ‘failure to check rampant drug addiction in the state’. AAP govt formed a four-member Special Investigation Team, headed by ADGP Naunihal Singh, on the family’s demand to probe his suicide. While the Mann govt has accused its rivals of politicising the issue and asserted that it has made arrests, there is no let-up in the political heat, with the opposition raising issues such as why Gulzar was shuttled between hospitals, whether he received adequate treatment, including ventilator support, and whether his family was pressured into cremating him. Congress on Tuesday carried out protests, while BJP too has been spearheading an agitation and is set to launch a statewide campaign against drugs. Opposition members have argued that their demand for Cheema’s resignation is aimed at ensuring a credible inquiry.

title: Today in Germany: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
description: Organised crime in Germany getting more international, digitally connected and violent, school pupils in Bavaria evacuated after chlorine gas leak, drone maker forced underground amid suspected Russian threat and more news on Wednesday.
content: Today's top story: Organised crime in Germany becoming more international and digitally connected Germany’s organised crime networks are becoming increasingly international, digitally connected and violent, according to the Federal Criminal Police Office's (BKA) latest report. The number of investigation proceedings into organised crime rose to 683 in 2025, the highest figure since 2021, while the number of suspects increased by more than 13 percent to 7,988 – also the highest level in five years. While presenting the findings, BKA Chief Holger Münch said: "Organised crime is changing its face: criminal networks today operate in a much more digitally interconnected, international and division-of-labour-based manner." Drug-related crime once again accounted for the vast majority of organised crime investigations during the reporting period, followed by economic crime, tax and customs offences, migrant smuggling, property crimes and money laundering. A total of 31 investigations focused primarily on violent crime. The BKA warned of an increase in extreme violence, including cases in which violent acts are commissioned as a service or carried out by minors recruited specifically for the purpose. Perpetrators are increasingly being recruited through social media, with some of those hired to carry out violent crimes as young as 13. Such criminal acts operate on the principle of "one plans, one pays, one carries out the attack," said Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) on Tuesday. Münch added that criminal networks today also "exploit geopolitical conflicts". READ ALSO: Which types of crime are rising in Germany? German drone maker goes underground amid suspected Russia threat Changing location every few weeks and constantly accompanied by body guards, the head of a German startup supplying drones to Ukraine has been forced into hiding due to a suspected Russian assassination plot. "Putin chose this path, and I have to accept that and respond accordingly," Stefan Thumann, CEO of German defence tech firm Donaustahl, told AFP in an interview from an undisclosed location. The 39-year believes that the saga will only end one of two ways – when "the Russian regime is toppled" or the Russians succeed in killing him, he said. Thumann is an outspoken supporter of Ukraine's war against President Vladimir Putin and a supplier of attack drones to Kyiv. Authorities first warned him last December that he could be in danger, he said. Soon after, "I was explicitly told that the threat comes from Russia and that a murder attempt on me is planned," he said. His life has been turned upside down by being forced to go underground, although he still manages to oversee his company's work. "I'm more or less completely isolated from the outside world," he said, adding that communication with family was "sporadic" and "only digital". Contacted by AFP, the interior ministry of the southern state of Bavaria – where Donaustahl is based – said it was aware of the case but declined to comment further, noting that it was under investigation by federal prosecutors. School pupils in Würzburg evacuated after gas leak Around 2,000 pupils were evacuated from a vocational school in Würzburg, Bavaria, on Tuesday due to a chlorine gas leak at the building's swimming pool. The incident happened shortly before 10am at the Franz-Oberthür School. Firefighters said two substances used to disinfect the pool had been combined – but because the swimming pool water was missing, the two agents triggered an unwanted chemical reaction. A total of 14 people were affected, with 10 taken to hospital mainly suffering from respiratory irritation. The fire service later gave the all-clear after emergency crews removed and neutralised the chemical mixture. Police are investigating the circumstances of the incident. German investor morale misses expectations as Mideast war weighs German investor sentiment rose much less than expected in September, a closely watched survey showed Tuesday, underscoring the economy's fragility as the Mideast war persists and suspected attacks on infrastructure unnerve investors. The ZEW institute's economic expectations index edged up just 0.5 points to 34.7, the survey found, its fifth rise in a row. That was far below forecasts of a 10-point increase in a poll of analysts by the financial platform FactSet. Expensive energy resulting from the US war against Iran and the near total closure of the Strait of Hormuz were weighing on sentiment, ZEW president Achim Wambach said. Petrol prices on Monday reached a record of €2.286 ($2.64) a litre in Germany as the war pushes up oil and gas prices worldwide. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Tuesday that the government "had to act" on fuel costs, adding that it would have concrete measures to announce "very soon". READ ALSO: Germany plans price relief for drivers amid rising fuel costs "The risks are nevertheless considerable," Wambach said, citing "high energy prices amid the ongoing war in Iran and further uncertainty caused by hybrid attacks are weighing on the economy". Berlin's run-down public spaces at heart of election campaign Politicians campaigning for Sunday's Berlin state election have painted an unflattering picture of the German capital, vowing to clear garbage-strewn streets and promising "syringe-free playgrounds". Town hall-hopefuls have also pledged to clean up graffiti-covered train stations, end "forever-building sites", fix buckled cycling lanes and take steps to ease a desperate shortage of affordable housing. Taken together, the list of woes hardens the image of a chronically broke city whose administration often struggles to reliably provide services for its almost four million people. READ ALSO: - Why is rubbish causing such a stink in the Berlin elections? - What foreign residents need to know about Berlin's upcoming election Certainly, many who live in Berlin love its rich artistic and cultural life, green spaces, lakes and children's playgrounds, vibrant start-up scene and hedonistic, anything-goes nightlife. But that has gone hand-in-hand with persistent complaints about a slow bureaucracy and dysfunctional services. Local newspapers often write about Berlin's "crime hotspots" and rising homelessness, and make great sport of documenting ever-new Berlin disasters – from rat-infested police stations to the closure of the Technical University's main campus due to structural defects and fire safety issues. A spokesperson for the City told AFP, when asked about the garbage problem, that there were "no operational failures", pointing instead to many residents' lack of civic responsibility. With reporting by AFP

title: How the great gas crisis of 2030 will play out
description: A speculative scenario set in October 2030 imagines a third global natural gas crisis in eight years, as faltering US shale output, extreme weather, AI data centres and LNG exports squeeze domestic supplies. Record gas prices hit farmers, manufacturers and ho…
content: After Russia’s invasion of Ukraine cut off Europe from two-fifths of its gas in 2022, importers reassured themselves that the Persian Gulf and the US had plenty to spare. Also read: Trump’s ‘little war’ with Iran just got a lot bigger When the 2026 war with Iran similarly knocked out 20% of global LNG supply, America’s booming fossil-fuel industry again promised to fill the gap. That confidence now seems shockingly naive. US natural gas prices have been caught in a perfect storm: Growth in shale output has been faltering. Season upon season of extreme weather has hit a power sector crippled by former President Donald Trump’s war on clean energy. Frontier AI labs, racing to beat a technological singularity they are warning is finally just months away, are sucking up fossil fuels to power data centers. Meanwhile, LNG terminals are allowing foreign buyers to compete directly with Americans habituated to rock-bottom prices. LNG exports found unlikely allies among Republicans watching one of the country’s great competitive advantages — cheap energy — disappear. Then came July’s heat dome. New Orleans recorded 70 heat-related deaths. Many were suburban retirees who had switched off air conditioners as electricity bills devoured half of their Social Security payments. On the day a new poll showed Louisiana Republican heavyweight and gas-export advocate Steve Scalise trailing a populist primary challenger by 11 points, Fox News broadcast footage of four LNG tankers departing the Gulf Coast bound for China. Within days, protestors carrying “It’s OUR gas” placards were outside Congress. That’s when all hell broke loose. European gas storage was already running dangerously low after the same torrid El Niño summer, leaving importers heavily dependent on US shipments. Japan and South Korea were even more exposed. After a bruising trade fight with Washington in 2027, both had restricted Chinese clean-energy imports in return for preferential access to US LNG. That slowed deployment of the technologies that might have now insulated them from the crisis. Russia was in no position to come to the rescue. Eight years of war in Ukraine, an economy approaching Venezuela-style degeneration and incessant hybrid-warfare attacks on its petroleum infrastructure had decimated its capacity to respond. The situation in the Gulf offered little reassurance. Relations between Qatar and Iran’s increasingly lawless government were deteriorating over the management of their vast shared offshore gas field, threatening the uneasy truce in Hormuz brokered after the 2028 US election. Then Iran’s Revolutionary Guards boarded a QatarEnergy LNG tanker and turned it back. Australia offered no respite either. The world’s biggest LNG exporter as recently as 2022 had imposed US-style export restrictions in 2026 to shield domestic supplies. Also read: Iran war cost hits $38 billion, forecast to rise $3 billion a month How did the world fail to see what seems so inevitable now? It was hardly unprecedented. In the 1970s, the US banned exports of soybeans and crude oil to protect consumers from rising prices. The oil ban lasted four decades before being lifted in 2015, sparking a production boom that eventually hardened into hubris about a new era of American energy dominance. The mistake was to believe the petroleum industry’s bromides about the stability of LNG — what Shell Plc described as the fuel’s “flexible and reliable energy security.” The poorer Asian countries hit hardest by the 2022 and 2026 crises look best-placed right now. Rather than betting their power systems on a fuel for which rich countries could always outbid them, countries from Pakistan to the Philippines accelerated investment in solar, batteries and domestic energy. Developed Asia and Europe, in contrast, conflated flexibility with security, and were slower to pivot. That was a disastrous choice. LNG can be shipped halfway around the world, but Russia, Qatar and now the US have each demonstrated how quickly politics can disrupt those flows. After three gas crises in eight years, perhaps the remarkable thing isn’t that countries are finally learning this. It’s that anyone still needed the lesson. title: Delhi-NCR, Haryana brace for rain, thunderstorms as active Western Disturbance affects region
description: Delhi and surrounding NCR areas are expected to experience cloudy skies and light rain. Isolated heavy rainfall and thunderstorms are forecast for Wednesday and Thursday. Gusty winds will accompany the weather activity across parts of Delhi-NCR. This wet spel…
content: NEW DELHI: Delhi is likely to see a generally cloudy sky with light rain and thunderstorms on Wednesday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting continued wet weather over the national capital, Gurugram and other parts of Delhi-NCR. The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab on Wednesday and Thursday. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely at isolated places, with gusty winds expected in parts of Delhi-NCR and Haryana. The weather activity is associated with an active Western Disturbance affecting northwest India, which is expected to bring spells of rain and thunderstorms to the region. Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 26.8 degrees Celsius on Wednesday. Lodi Road recorded 26.2 degrees Celsius, 2.2 degrees above normal, while Ayanagar recorded 25.8 degrees Celsius, 1.4 degrees above normal. Palam recorded 25.2 degrees Celsius, 0.3 degrees above normal. The Ridge recorded the lowest minimum temperature at 22.8 degrees Celsius, 1.4 degrees below normal. No rainfall was recorded at Safdarjung, Palam, Lodi Road and Ayanagar in the 24 hours preceding Wednesday morning, while the Ridge recorded trace rainfall, according to the IMD. The weather office said the rainfall activity is likely to occur in spells, accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds, rather than as continuous rain through the day. The wet spell is expected to continue into Thursday, with fairly widespread to widespread rainfall forecast over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh and Punjab. The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms and lightning at isolated places in Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab and Uttarakhand. Isolated heavy rainfall is likely over several other regions, including Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Meanwhile, Delhi's air quality remained in the "satisfactory" category, with the city's AQI recorded at 98 at 9am on Wednesday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board.
